543300|2026-06.headline: Sona Comstar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23.1% on input-cost inflation and pass-through lag.
543300|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore, with BEV revenue up 107% to ₹436 crore and BEV share of automotive sales at 44%, both described as the best ever. EBITDA rose 49% to ₹303 crore but margin contracted about 0.7 pp to 23.1%, with April and May weak and June better on pass-through recoveries. PAT grew 45% to ₹181 crore (13.6% margin). Management framed the quarter alongside the Denso JV announcement (two JVs: high-voltage/hybrid for 4W and 2/3W electrification) and a new Robotics and Physical AI vertical with ₹800 crore order book.

financial_highlights.metric: BEV share of automotive product sales

segments.name: Electrification (BEV)
segments.commentary: BEV revenue ₹436 crore, +107% YoY, highest ever BEV mix; EV order book at 69 programmes across 36 customers after 2 new EV and 1 hybrid programme.

segments.name: Traction motors / suspension motors
segments.commentary: Traction motors had the fastest growth in the quarter along with EV suspension motors (management ranked suspension motors fastest in growth); traction motors carry lowest margin and diluted group margin.

segments.name: Driveline / ICE differential gears
segments.commentary: Won ₹2.1 billion ICE differential gear programme from a North American OEM; new hybrid differential assembly order from an existing North American customer.

segments.name: Robotics and Physical AI
segments.commentary: Three new orders adding ₹6 billion, taking the vertical's order book to ₹8 billion; first product (AMR) prototype shown at CES; one SOP in Q1 FY28 per management timing guidance.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Railway acquisition in first year of post-acquisition integration; additional railway business wins noted, no revenue split disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Margin recovery expected to become progressively more visible from Q2 FY27 as cost pass-throughs catch up; June showed significant improvement over April-May.
Management said material-cost pass-through lag and revenue/cost arithmetic may keep pressure on margin percentage in the near term.
Expects phenomenal EV growth in India and Europe-led electrification to continue through the year, though US EV demand is weak.
Robotics orders: one SOP this quarter, one next quarter, one within 15 months; management said the market is developing faster than internal assumptions.
JV2 (high voltage) SOP timeline not disclosed due to confidentiality; JV1 expected to kick off faster than JV2.
capex_capacity: Management said it has no capacity constraint; OEM constraints are supply-chain driven, and capacity is built ahead of markets.
Denso JV2 (high voltage 4W/CV electrification) is Denso majority-owned with Denso leading management; JV1 (2/3W) is Sona majority-owned with Sona management control and licenses technology to the JV.
Management cited capex intensity thumb rule of ₹8-9 revenue per ₹1 capex for high-voltage systems, and at least ₹11-12 per ₹1 capex per Sat Mohan Gupta.
Suspension, motor and non-traction motor businesses are outside the Denso JV scope.
Robotics products under commercialisation include short-range radar sensors and advanced robotic components; AMR platform in development.
demand_pricing: Demand healthy across markets: India strong (passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers), Europe growing, US improved through the quarter, China mixed but fastest-growing geography for the company due to suspension motor ramp-up.
Management said EV volumes are constrained by OEM supply chains rather than demand.
Input cost inflation (commodities, labour) was the main margin headwind; April and May were tough, June improved.
Rare earth: heavy rare earth magnets remain restricted from import; company has shifted to light rare earth alternatives with no magnet shortage for traction motors.
Management described high-voltage motor competition as less intense than 2/3W due to technology barriers.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about AI/robotics economics, software share of value, and capital commitment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said metal plus software is now standard across products; suspension motors carry 2 million lines of code. Robotics entry has three revenue streams: components, perception engineering services, and full platforms (AMRs and cobots); no capex guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for JV2 revenue and capacity/TAM sizing for high-voltage JV?
qa_highlights.answer: SOP timelines withheld under confidentiality; JV1 to lead and JV2 to follow. Denso electrification revenue above $8 billion a year; Indian hybrid/EV car and CV addressable market ~2.3 million vehicles, about ₹24,000 crore by 2030 and roughly 3x that by 2035 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why put 2/3W traction motors into JV1 when already growing well?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Denso's interest, access to customers currently not open, export opportunities where Denso is dominant, and a single strategic intent across both JVs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-axle in JV1 but not JV2?
qa_highlights.answer: JV2 makes motors and inverters; e-axle (motor, inverter, gearbox integration) is a tiny market for JV1 and can be sold to e-axle makers, OEMs, or Sona driveline.

qa_highlights.question: Why is VA-to-employee ratio declining QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to product mix shift toward assembly businesses (motors, railways) vs driveline; ratio at 4.5x is still strong and varies quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When do robotics orders start production?
qa_highlights.answer: One starts this quarter, one next quarter, and one within about 15 months; most within 12-15 months.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery: whether EBITDA margin improvement from pass-through shows in Q2 FY27 as management guided.
Traction motor mix: lowest-margin product growing fastest, a continuing dilution to group margin.
Execution risk on Denso JV1 and JV2: SOP timing not disclosed; capex and royalty economics not quantified.
Robotics: early-stage, ₹8 billion order book, product life cycles and generational change unclear to management as well.
Rare earth magnet restriction on heavy rare earths; company relies on light rare earth alternatives.
US EV demand weakness and OEM supply-chain bottlenecks limiting volumes.
543300|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, electrification and new partnerships; cautious on near-term margins, explicitly attributing pressure to input inflation and pass-through lag. Evasive on JV timelines, JV2 revenue sizing and Denso's own India supply, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: I'm happy to share this was the best ever quarter for revenue, BEV revenue, and BEV revenue share, with very healthy momentum, continuing across the business.
Margins were heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases as well as the timing gap in the customer recoveries or the pass-throughs.
EV is in a way, right now, we are not constrained by demand. Actually, all our OEMs are not constrained by demand. They are constrained by their own supply chain challenges.
Our suspension motor product has 2 million lines of code. Almost nothing we make today is just metal, it is metal and a few lines of code.
Denso is not a leader, it is by far the runaway leader when it comes to hybrid powertrains. The electrification business revenue for Denso is above $8 billion a year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell about 0.7 pp to 23.1% on input-cost inflation and pass-through lag, but June improved over April-May and management guided recovery to become progressively more visible from Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: JV1 first, JV2 later; SOP timing not disclosed
rows.why: Denso JV1 (2/3W) is expected to kick off faster than JV2 (high voltage), and robotics has one SOP in Q1 FY28, but no plant capacity figures or dates were given and management said it has no capacity constraint.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue grew 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore, the net order book is ₹24,000 crore with EVs at 64%, and the EV book reached 69 programmes across 36 customers, though management flagged US EV weakness and supply-chain limits.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it has no capacity constraint and builds capacity ahead of markets, and the Denso JVs and robotics ramp will need capex, but no capex amount or plan was quantified and JV economics were withheld.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance was raised or given numerically; only qualitative margin recovery was discussed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management said material-cost pass-through lag may keep pressure on margin percentage in the near term, with April and May weak, so the Q2 recovery depends on pass-through catching up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Robotics has one SOP this quarter, one next quarter and one within 15 months, with the AMR platform still in development, and the ₹2.1 billion ICE differential gear programme and JV1 are also in the pipeline.

rows.label: Robotics order book to ₹8 billion
rows.why: Three new orders added ₹6 billion, lifting the vertical's order book to ₹8 billion, with one SOP this quarter and one next quarter.

rows.label: EV programme wins and BEV mix
rows.why: BEV revenue rose 107% YoY to ₹436 crore, 44% of automotive product sales, with 2 new EV and 1 hybrid programme added and India and Europe EV growth expected to continue.

rows.label: Cost pass-through recovery
rows.why: June margins improved over April-May as cost pass-throughs began to recover, and management expects this to become more visible from Q2 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on EV growth, the Denso JVs and robotics orders, but cautious on near-term margins; the brief notes evasiveness on JV timelines and JV2 revenue sizing, which the analysts pressed on.

543300|2026-09.headline: Sona Comstar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹1,546 crore and EBITDA to ₹356 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23% on mix and input costs.
543300|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set company records for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with BEV revenue up 129% YoY and above 50% of automotive revenue for the first time. Margins were lower YoY: EBITDA margin 23% (down 2.3 pp) on traction motor mix shift and West Asia-linked input inflation. Order additions of ₹36 billion (third highest quarter) took the net order book to ₹251 billion, the second highest ever. Management kept the 23-25% EBITDA margin range and flagged the Denso JV closings (JV1 targeted by end-December 2026, JV2 in 1H CY2027).

segments.name: BEV / EV business
segments.commentary: BEV revenue grew 129% YoY and 40% QoQ, and was 51% of automotive product sales in Q2; H1 BEV revenue ₹1,042 crore (+119%). Two-wheeler and three-wheeler demand in India was the main driver.

segments.name: Traction motors
segments.commentary: Business grew about 50% QoQ, faster than management expected; driven by both wallet-share gains at existing OEMs and market growth, and it is the main reason for the margin dilution.

segments.name: EV suspension motors
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing product, reported at about 7% of revenue; its order book so far is with a single customer, with other OEM talks ongoing.

segments.name: Differential assemblies and gears (DA + DG)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue up 37% YoY; all three large EV DA customers picked up in Q2. Entered ICE passenger-car differential assembly with an existing gear customer.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Air springs supplied for the first time this quarter and ramping; first batch of HVAC systems supplied in FY27; electric panels in early ramp-up.

segments.name: Geography and mix
segments.commentary: Eastern markets are about 2/3 of revenue, up from about 1/3 two years ago. Two/three-wheelers are 14% of revenue; auto vs non-auto split 70:30.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin range of 23-25% retained for now; management expects about 23% in a normal macro scenario and says it will hold unless oil reaches about $150.
Margin direction depends on traction motor mix (lower-margin product) and on whether material prices stay high, flat or fall.
JV1 (carve-out of business) targeted to close by end-December 2026, possibly slipping into January 2027; JV2 not yet formed, targeted for 1H CY2027.
Management reiterated a long-term aspiration implying about 25% revenue CAGR, targeting 10x growth over 10 years under Sona Comstar 2.0.

Net cash could reach roughly ₹2,800-3,000 crore by year end if the Denso JV proceeds of about ₹900 crore are received, per analyst arithmetic; management said tax, capex and JV2 capex will absorb part of this.
M&A remains selective; cash-to-EBITDA ratio ceiling of about 1.5x is the stated threshold before deploying cash.
capex_capacity: ₹62 crore of capex declared last quarter for robotics and physical AI, per management.
Helical limited slip differential, air springs for railways and rear radar sensor for two-wheelers commercialised in Q2; three new products in the quarter, a record.

Capacity and capability to ramp fast were cited in the context of traction motor demand; heavy rare earth magnets are unavailable due to Chinese export restrictions, and the company moved to light rare earth alternatives.
AMRs developed in-house are being deployed on Sona factory floors for use-case development.
Robotics and physical AI order book about 4% of the ₹251 billion total order book.
demand_pricing: Q2 order additions ₹36 billion, the third highest quarter; net order book ₹251 billion, the second highest in company history; wins spread across differentials, gears, traction motors, controllers, starter motors, sensors and railways.
Four new EPIC programs in Q2 (3 BEV, 1 intelligent and connected); 75 EPIC programs across 37 customers at end-H1, of which 44 are in production and 31 yet to start.
Inflation: steel, copper and oil derivatives rose on West Asia conflict; freight rates nearly doubled QoQ.
Pass-through contracts exist with customers but lag the input cost increases, and the percentage margin falls arithmetically when costs rise and are passed through.
Europe: OEMs seeking an alternative supply chain to China, and the company is winning more European business.
Management said it is not taking customer-specific questions.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the suspension motor growth, and what is the order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product's trajectory is hard to predict; the first launch customer's model underperformed then its new model exceeded expectations. Order book is still limited to one customer, with significant talks with other OEMs; no quantified pipeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Denso JV timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: JV1 (carve-out) targeted to close by end-December 2026, possibly January 2027. JV2 not yet formed, targeted for 1H CY2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is traction motor growth above industry growth, and what is the three-wheeler contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both wallet-share gains and market growth, plus OEM supply-chain difficulties that favoured the company's agility. Three-wheeler contribution was not quantified; a further product launch is planned this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold at 23-25% given mix shift and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the 23-25% range. CFO said about 23% is the ballpark in a normal scenario and product mix is the key determinant; material price flattening would support margins, further sharp increases would hurt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and M&A plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross cash ₹1,966 crore, net ₹1,400-1,500 crore. M&A is selective (three deals in the last decade), with four filters: 15-year product life, top 5-10 global position, margin and return accretion, and moral good. Cash-to-EBITDA ceiling of about 1.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Robotics and humanoid R&D spend, timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is in-house, mostly staff time; ₹62 crore capex is earmarked for the area. Management will demonstrate at Bharat Expo in February 2027. No inflection year was forecast; the curve is expected to be steep when it arrives.

risks_watch: Continued margin compression from traction motor mix shift and lagged pass-through of steel, copper and oil-linked inflation, with freight costs nearly doubled QoQ.
Suspension motor growth depends on a single customer so far; other OEM wins still to be secured.
Heavy rare earth export restrictions from China remain in place with no sign of easing.
Denso JV timing could slip (JV1 into January 2027; JV2 not until 1H CY2027).
Management flagged near-term predictability as difficult due to West Asia inflation.
Railway growth outlook not quantified; depends on timely new-product launches.
543300|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, orders and cash flow, with the mood set as a near-perfect quarter. More cautious on margins and input costs, where management explicitly said near-term predictability is limited and declined to give forward growth figures for railways or robotics.
key_quotes: Q2 was almost a perfect quarter for us across all metrics - financial performance, new order wins, technology and new products, cash flow generation, and our total quality management.
Traction motor demand has significantly exceeded even our own internal expectations.
And M&A is the right way to look at it. Just because everyone is doing it, is not the reason we will do it.
Whenever it does come, the curve will be very steep. That is something I can guarantee.

financial_highlights.change: +35% YoY; +18% QoQ vs previous record ₹1,310 crore
90% of H1 EBITDA; ₹44 crore working capital release
More than 50% above full FY26 FCF

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 23% (down 2.3 pp YoY) on traction motor mix and lagged pass-through; management keeps 23-25% range and sees about 23% in a normal scenario, so expansion depends on material prices flattening or falling.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line quantified; management cites capability to ramp traction motors with agility, and traction motor business grew about 50% QoQ, so capacity additions are not disclosed and remain unconfirmed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue up 35% YoY to ₹1,546 crore, net order book ₹251 bn (second highest ever), 75 EPIC programs across 37 customers with 31 yet to start, and BEV revenue up 129% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H1 capex only about ₹148 crore and ₹62 crore robotics capex already declared; utilisation not disclosed, so no high-utilisation trigger is evident, though the 1.5x cash-to-EBITDA ceiling leaves room for M&A or capex deployment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 23-25% EBITDA margin range and gave no revenue guidance raise, and said near-term predictability is limited by West Asia inflation.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin fell 2.3 pp YoY to 23%, steel, copper and freight (nearly doubled QoQ) inflation is lagging pass-through, and management said margins hold only unless oil reaches about $150.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Three new products commercialised in Q2 (helical LSD, railway air springs, rear radar sensor), a further product launch is planned this quarter, and the Bharat Expo demo is set for February 2027.

rows.label: Denso JV1 carve-out closing
rows.why: Management targets JV1 closing by end-December 2026, with about ₹900 crore of JV proceeds expected per analyst arithmetic, though timing could slip into January 2027.

rows.label: EV suspension motor OEM wins
rows.why: Suspension motors about 7% of revenue and the fastest-growing product, but the order book sits with a single customer, with significant talks with other OEMs and no quantified pipeline.

rows.label: Europe supply-chain diversification wins
rows.why: OEMs seeking alternatives to China and the company is winning more European business, but no figures were given; eastern markets are about 2/3 of revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, orders (₹251 bn book), BEV growth and cash flow, but cautious on margins and input costs, saying near-term predictability is limited; analysts pressed on margin sustainability with mix shift and inflation, and on the suspension motor pipeline.

543306|2026-03.headline: Dodla Dairy Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR1,074 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 5% as milk procurement costs outran price hikes.
543306|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR1,074 crore (+18.1% YoY) on volume growth, but EBITDA margin compressed to 5% as procurement cost rose to INR41/litre from INR37.4 a year earlier while average milk sales price moved only to INR58.4/litre. Reported Q4 PAT of INR70 crore (6.5% margin) was flattered by about INR39 crore of one-offs; underlying Q4 PAT is about INR40 crore. FY26 adjusted PAT is about INR215 crore (5.2% margin) against reported INR267 crore. Management guides to a gradual 50-100 bps gross margin recovery in FY27 and low-to-mid-teens revenue growth, with procurement relief expected from June.

segments.name: India standalone
segments.commentary: Q4 milk procurement averaged 18.5 lakh litres/day (+13.4% YoY); procurement cost INR41/litre vs INR37.4 a year ago, and average milk sales price INR58.4/litre vs INR57.7 in Q3. Standalone India EBITDA margin for FY26 was about 6-7%, with Q4 described as a cyclical trough.

segments.name: Value-added products (VAP)
segments.commentary: Total VAP INR2,969 million vs INR2,841 million in Q4 FY25; excluding bulk sales, VAP grew 21% YoY. Curd rupee sales were INR230 crore in Q4 and INR845.7 crore in FY26; consolidated VAP realisation was INR60.54/litre.

segments.name: Africa (Uganda and Kenya)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR151 crore (+48% YoY) with liquid milk volume up more than 60%; record quarterly EBITDA of INR18 crore. FY26 EBITDA margin about 11.3% vs 11% in FY25, and FY26 volume about 2.27 lakh litres/day (Uganda about 1.5 lakh, Kenya about 0.9 lakh).

segments.name: OSAM / HR Food (OrgaFeed)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR81.9 crore (+23.2% YoY) with EBITDA INR2.7 crore; FY26 revenue INR214.7 crore and EBITDA INR4.8 crore. Management cites about 21% gross margin, targeting 25%, and a 6-12 month window to converge with company margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided to low-to-mid teens, supported by full-year OSAM consolidation, Africa on current trajectory, and 8-9% organic growth in India.
Gross margin to recover 50-100 bps over FY26 levels as procurement normalises and pricing actions take effect.
Effective tax rate to return to 25-27% after favourable ITAT orders in FY26; no further tax-credit impact from Q1 FY27.
Africa to reach 15-18% of consolidated revenue by FY28; Africa volume growth of about 20% targeted, implying about INR600 crore revenue vs about INR500 crore in FY26.
Management expects procurement to fall by roughly INR1-1.5/litre and a further rupee or so of price correction, with Q1 FY27 standalone margin recovery.
Capital allocation priority: growth capex (Maharashtra, Uganda, regular capex) from internal accruals, then regular dividends, then selective bolt-on acquisitions.
capex_capacity: Maharashtra project (total envelope INR280 crore): INR20 crore spent in FY25, INR86 crore in FY26, and about INR180 crore planned in FY27; commercial operations expected by end FY27.
FY27 standalone capex budget about INR130 crore, including INR65 crore regular capex and about INR7 crore hardware (excluding Maharashtra).
Uganda greenfield: 70 acres acquired, total capex about INR60 crore including land and plant, phased, completion by end FY29; Phase 2 adds pasteurised milk and milk products.
Bihar: 7-acre land allotted by BIADA for a dairy, with about INR4.4 crore land cost; subject to Board approval.
Maharashtra procurement averages about 3 lakh litres/day, with a target of at least 5 lakh litres/day by end of the season (around end of FY27).
demand_pricing: Company raised prices in mid-March 2026; cooperatives (Amul, Mother Dairy) followed with about INR2/litre hikes in May. Management says the next price action depends on fuel, packaging and freight stabilising, with only minor corrections planned in the near term.
Packaging material costs are up about 30% YoY (mainly plastics); expected to stay elevated as government excise support is temporary.
Freight: fuel up about INR3 recently; management said it will absorb for 15-30 days before passing on, with an estimated impact of about 0.25-0.5%.
Milk volume growth guided at 5-6% for liquid milk (about 9.4% including VAP in FY26); VAP growing 16-17% in the current season.
Procurement cost in mid-May was unchanged from March levels (INR41 consolidated, +9.7% YoY); the company says it has passed on about INR1/litre of the inflation so far.
Realisations: India milk INR58.25 vs INR56.15 YoY; HR Food milk INR55.7 and VAP INR98.8 vs Dodla India VAP INR64.2 (excluding fat products).
Management expects VAP mix to rise to 32-34% of revenue once expansions stabilise; seasonality in curd, buttermilk and lassi being addressed to extend demand from 2-3 months to about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin in this environment, and is the structural margin lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described FY27 as a cautious, transition year given fuel, plastic and agri-input uncertainty, and said margins can return to normal afterwards; another analyst confirmed the company expects margins to revert to mean by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is procurement cost today versus the Q4 average, and how much inflation has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement remains near March levels at about INR41/litre (+9.7% YoY consolidated, +9.3% standalone). About INR1/litre of inflation has been recovered so far, with another INR1-1.5 expected from procurement relief.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakup, and what were Q4 realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 standalone capex about INR130 crore plus Maharashtra INR180 crore. Q4 consolidated realisation was INR61.19 per litre (INR56.16 for milk), and VAP realisation INR60.54 consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How is OSAM margin expected to converge, and why did OrgaFeed margins drop?
qa_highlights.answer: OSAM margin improvement expected in 6-12 months via SAP, quality and logistics work, targeting about 25% gross margin. OrgaFeed margins fell from higher maize costs and freight for longer distances, but management says the margin is still about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa split by country and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 volume about 1.8 lakh litres/day (Uganda about 1.45 lakh, Kenya about 35,000); FY26 about 2.27 lakh (Uganda about 1.5 lakh, Kenya about 90,000). EBITDA margin about 11% in FY25 and 11.3% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How has the price-and-volume mix shifted in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquid milk volume grew about 5-6% YoY, VAP about 16%. Management says the company did not raise milk prices to protect market share and wants to keep the gap to cooperatives manageable.

risks_watch: Procurement normalisation is not yet visible: mid-May cost is unchanged, and the May-June recovery depends on Maharashtra and Karnataka productivity gains and on the southern states.
El Nino, drought and fuel price volatility (crude moves cited at USD60-120/barrel) could raise procurement, freight and packaging costs faster than prices can be passed on.
Q4 was flattered by about INR39 crore of one-offs (tax credit INR29 crore, interest income INR10 crore); FY27 PAT should be judged against about INR215 crore adjusted FY26.
OSAM and OrgaFeed margins are below the company average and depend on the pace of the SAP, logistics and procurement fixes.

Maharashtra greenfield (about INR180 crore to spend in FY27) and Uganda phase 2 raise execution risk and employee and other costs, which rose about 27% YoY in Q4 (employee) and about 15% (other expenses).
543306|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on medium-term recovery and Africa growth, but cautious on near-term margins; management repeatedly stressed uncertainty over fuel, packaging and El Nino and chose to guide conservatively. Some answers were unclear or required clarification during the call.

financial_highlights.change: Includes INR29 crore tax credit and INR10 crore interest income; underlying about INR40 crore
Adjusted about INR215 crore, 5.2% margin after about INR70 crore one-offs
Includes INR271 crore HR Food expansion, INR86 crore Maharashtra, INR73 crore maintenance

key_quotes: Margins remained under pressure due to elevated milk procurement costs and a calibrated pricing strategy.
Going forward, the situation is turning positive. Milk supply is improving, which should result in a normalization of procurement costs for milk sales.
So this is more a '27 year kind of a year where, taking into consideration uncertainties versus what is going on, that we are trying to give this kind of a guidance.
Excluding these two one -off items, our Q4 underlying PAT is approximately INR40 crores.
This is the clean baseline against which FY '27 should be evaluated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: Q1 FY27 onward, gradual over FY27
rows.why: Management guides 50-100 bps gross margin recovery over FY26 levels as procurement falls INR1-1.5/litre from INR41 and about INR1/litre of price has been passed on so far, though mid-May procurement is still unchanged at INR41 and Q4 EBITDA margin was only 5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Maharashtra dairy under construction within a INR280 crore envelope, about INR180 crore to spend in FY27 with commercial operations by end FY27; Maharashtra procurement at about 3 lakh litres/day is targeted to reach at least 5 lakh/day.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Liquid milk volume guided at 5-6% and VAP growing 16-17% this season; Africa volume targeted up about 20% from 2.27 lakh litres/day and India organic growth 8-9% in FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone FY27 capex budget of about INR130 crore is set, Uganda greenfield (INR60 crore, 70 acres) is approved, and Bihar land (7 acres, INR4.4 crore) is allotted subject to Board approval, so a formal Board capex step for Bihar is the next likely trigger; utilisation not disclosed.

543308|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR 1,075 crore, but EBITDA pre-Ind AS fell 33.5% to INR 131 crore as new hospitals dragged margins.
543308|2026-03.overview: KIMS reported Q4 FY26 total revenue of INR 1,084 crore (+35.3% YoY, +8.1% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 216 crore (+6.8% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 19.9% versus 25.3% a year ago. Management attributed the margin compression to roughly INR 32 crore of EBITDA erosion from newer units (in operation under one year), while mature units held about 28.5-29% margins. PAT fell to INR 33 crore from INR 106 crore a year ago. Management is raising about INR 1,500 crore via QIP to cut net debt, which it says has peaked at INR 3,000-plus crore, and targets net debt to EBITDA of 1-2x from about 1x-3x currently.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is near INR 3,000-plus crore and the QIP will retire debt, with cash flow then funding 3-5 year greenfield projects. Expansion plans are still being explored; 400-500 beds of small acquisitions may come in the next two quarters, all in home markets.

qa_highlights.answer: Nashik still needs STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA. Thane has GIPSA, with Medi Assist and STAR nearly done, covering about 70% of insurance volume. Bangalore needs 3-4 more months. Confusion from the new GIC common-empanelment process caused the delays.

qa_highlights.answer: The 800-bed Kondapur facility is almost fully capex-complete, with INR 50-75 crore left for two additional floors in FY28-FY29. Phase 1 covers 400-500 beds. Transition cost is expected to be about INR 15-25 crore, based on the Sunshine move precedent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt outlook for FY27 after the QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,000 crore of debt to be retired from QIP proceeds. The balance covers losses at new hospitals and capex in existing facilities.

543317|2026-03.headline: G R Infra Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 27% YoY to INR2,521 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to ~11% from 15.5%.
543317|2026-03.overview: Standalone revenue grew 27% YoY to about INR2,521 crore in Q4 FY26 and 17% to INR7,620 crore for FY26, driven by oil and gas and power transmission execution. Margins compressed on higher construction costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at ~10.85% in Q4 versus 17.5% a year earlier, which included a one-time claim of INR47.5 crore. Execution slipped in March owing to a delayed appointed date on one project and geopolitical-driven fuel and bitumen price volatility, with oil and gas revenue of ~INR400-450 crore against an internal expectation of ~INR600 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of ~15% and new order wins of INR20,000-22,000 crore, while order book stands at ~INR26,470 crore.

segments.commentary: Dining-out and movies are the largest categories, with retail stores and events the more promising newer ones. Customer base is smaller than food delivery or quick commerce, with fewer cities and higher NAOV.

segments.name: Nugget (enterprise AI)
segments.commentary: Management described it as in stealth mode with good traction. Losses rose on manpower, and no GPU spend was cited. More detail is to come in a couple of quarters.

guidance_outlook: Blinkit long-term margin is now expected at the higher end of the prior range, and the quick commerce long-term guidance was raised to 6% from 5-6%.
Long-term GAAP EBIT margin of about 4% for Blinkit, after ESOP and depreciation; adjusted EBITDA close to 6%.
Blinkit NAOV is expected to stay in the same range, and may rise again in Q3 on seasonality, but not meaningfully.
Management gave no guidance on Q2 Blinkit volume growth.
Management said no near-term margin pressure is expected, and margins should continue to improve as growth continues.
capex_capacity: Capex per store is now INR 2.5 crore (includes warehousing), vs INR 1 crore earlier; lumpy, and capex per store over 6-9 months is said to be below INR 2.5 crore.
About 200 Blinkit stores added in Q1, with quarterly capex around INR 700 crore.
Shifting to larger stores; new-format stores are cited at 2,100-2,200 orders per day, and existing stores are being upgraded to larger properties.
Bistro is adding about 10 kitchens per quarter, with more aggressive expansion planned later.
Management said NOV per store per day rose about 60% against the earlier assumption, versus about 150% for capex per store.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity in Q1 was the peak seen so far; competitors are subsidising grocery and delivery fees, and management sees limited room to go deeper.
Blinkit NAOV is flat YoY. Management said mix, assortment and price matching drive NAOV, and it is not a focus metric.
Blinkit retention and cohort spend: older cohorts spend about 3x versus three years earlier, mostly through frequency; the figure covers the full cohort, including churned customers.
Blinkit growth is mostly from existing cities; non-metros are growing faster on a smaller base.
Quick commerce MTU pareto is much flatter than food delivery (top 15-18% of customers drive 80% of revenue in food delivery).
Management said the pricing-led strategy is not sustainable, and that discounting is less effective in quick commerce than in e-commerce due to limited shelf space in dark stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise the quick commerce long-term margin guidance to 6% amid competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said capex per store and efficiency gains, plus larger store sizes, give higher margin visibility, so the company expects to finish at the higher end of the earlier range.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 the peak of competitive intensity, and what does predictability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Albinder Singh Dhindsa said Q1 was the peak seen to date because more players were aggressive. Competition now mainly takes the form of product and delivery-fee subsidies, which he said cannot go much deeper without large losses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit AOV fall for two quarters, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop is in line with last year and mostly reflects category mix and price matching. NAOV is an outcome, flat YoY, and not expected to grow meaningfully. Q3 may rise on seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit contribution margin not rise with take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher minimum wages in several states and larger new stores with lower early contribution. Q1 last-mile costs are seasonally high, and YoY gross profit gains have largely flowed to contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Blinkit capex around INR 700 crore for 200 stores when the stated capex per store is INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said warehouse capex is lumpy, so the per-store figure should be read over 6-9 months or longer. Over those periods capex per store is below INR 2.5 crore, and management expects that to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the net working capital reduction to 14 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said lower inventory days, from better replenishment and throughput, drove the cut from 18 to 14 days, with a steady-state target of 12 days. Kunal Swarup said the Q1 OCF lift came from a one-off tax refund on higher advance tax.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the slight dip in food delivery restaurant count?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal attributed the dip to the LPG situation last quarter, which took some restaurants offline. He did not cite rationalisation.

risks_watch: Competition from Toing and Ownly in food delivery, and quick commerce subsidy intensity, which could put pressure on margins or MTU growth.
Q2 Blinkit volume trends, since no guidance was given; the analyst's historical 18-20% 1Q-to-2Q range was not addressed.
Blinkit contribution margin trajectory as store formats and minimum wages change; Q1 was described as seasonally weak.
Inventory losses held at about 1.8% of NOV, with management not expecting much improvement.
Capex intensity and ROCE: EBIT margin is currently negative, so there is no ROCE yet; management said the company will accept lower margins if ROCE holds.
Nugget losses (manpower-driven) and limited disclosure; Bistro is expanding cautiously, with unit economics still being proven.
Payables growth (about INR 1,650 crore QoQ increase) and whether terms with brands are improving; management said it is scale-driven.

543320|2026-09.headline: Eternal's Q2FY27 call was Q&A-only: management kept FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance and flagged food margins flat for 1-2 years while reinvesting in growth.
543320|2026-09.overview: The call covered only the Q&A session, with no prepared remarks or reported financial figures in the transcript. Management said competitive intensity in food delivery rose in Q2 and that Eternal is investing more in customer acquisition and frequency, with margins expected to stay broadly flat over the next 1-2 years. In quick commerce, management said the 12-month competitive spike is over, which gives it confidence to re-accelerate store expansion, mainly in smaller cities, starting October-December quarter. Management also discussed dark.ai, a privacy-focused AI application for power users, which is unmonetised and carried in the Others segment.

Store capex guidance of INR 2.5 crore is a blended figure.

guidance_outlook: Management maintains the FY29 $1 billion Adjusted EBITDA guidance, but said it is too early to comment on it further.
Food delivery margins are expected to remain broadly flattish over the next 1-2 years, with investment in growth prioritised over margin optimisation.
Quick commerce store additions are to accelerate from the October-December quarter, with NOV growth expected to pick up on a YoY basis in that quarter.
Management expects the bulk of new quick commerce stores to be in smaller cities, and expects Blinkit's NOV per store per day to rise over time, though not linearly.
dark.ai launch is a few months away; monetisation and capex decisions will be taken closer to launch.

dark.ai capex is not expected to be meaningful unless the product gets a very strong response, in which case GPUs and infrastructure may be needed.

demand_pricing: Food delivery competitive intensity was higher in Q2, and Eternal is raising investment in new customer acquisition and frequency.
Quick commerce competition rose over the past 12 months with 5-7 players; management says it now has better visibility on competitor strategies.
Blinkit NOV growth is expected to pick up YoY from the October-December quarter. Blinkit's MTU in mature cities is multiple times Zomato's MTU, with no plateau seen yet.

qa_highlights.question: Has food delivery discounting intensified in Q2, and have margins peaked?
qa_highlights.answer: Competitive intensity was higher than in prior quarters, partly driven by Zomato. Management expects margins to stay broadly flattish over 1-2 years and to reinvest surplus in growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why accelerate quick commerce store additions in FY28, and where?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is now more predictable after the 12-month spike. Most new stores will be in smaller cities, where payback is described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Blinkit contribution margin trend despite NOV per store rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed flat contribution to investment in new stores. NOV per store does not translate linearly into contribution because store size and gross profit mix also vary.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance more comfortable given better competition visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment beyond maintaining the guidance, noting that only two quarters of the three-year plan have passed.

qa_highlights.question: What is dark.ai, what is its capex and monetisation, and is it within Eternal?
qa_highlights.answer: dark.ai is inside Eternal and unmonetised, with costs carried in Others. It is an application layer on open-source models, with the base case being a high gross margin, self-funding business. Hosting may need GPUs if demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will tier 2 and tier 3 store capex be below INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 2.5 crore figure is blended across tiers, set with the expectation that most expansion would be in tier 2 cities.

Blinkit store expansion could weigh on contribution margins in the short term and on NOV per store if new-store ramp is slower.

Share of NOV from top 8 cities is declining; management did not disclose the figure, so the mix shift is hard to track.
Exchange-rate exposure on dollar-priced tech server costs below contribution could raise indirect costs as the business scales.

543321|2026-03.headline: Tatva Chintan Q4 FY26 operating revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,341 million, with EBITDA of INR281 million (about 21% margin); FY27 guidance held at ~25% growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin.
543321|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR1,341 million, up 24% YoY and 2% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR281 million, up 214% YoY and 10% QoQ, which management attributed to better product mix and operating leverage. Electrolyte Salts was the standout segment, at INR131 million (up 1,378% YoY), while PTC fell 20% YoY and PASC fell 24% QoQ on dispatch delays after the new Dahej block was commissioned. Management maintained FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin despite raw-material and freight cost inflation linked to the geopolitical conflict, which is being partly passed on to customers. The Jolva greenfield project is set to break ground within about 60 days, with commercial production targeted for early 2028.

543325|2026-03.headline: Rolex Rings FY26 revenue held flat at INR1,144 crore despite a ~30% U.S. export drop; FY27 guided to 15-17% growth.
543325|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was about INR1,144 crore, broadly flat year on year, as a roughly 30% fall in U.S. exports was offset by Europe growth of about 25% and domestic growth of about 50%. Gross margin rose to 51.5% from 49.4%, attributed mainly to product mix, and operating EBITDA was held above 20%. Q4 other expenses were inflated by about INR22 crore of U.S. customs duty (about half recoverable from customers) and about INR6 crore of one-time legal and professional costs tied to the lender settlement. The company completed the INR101 crore Right of Recompense payment to lenders on March 31, 2026, and announced a INR180 crore buyback at INR180 per share, from which promoters are not participating.

543325|2026-06.headline: Rolex Rings Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4.3% to INR304 crore on labour-constrained output, while EBITDA margin expanded to 22.6% and PAT grew 22% to INR60 crore.
543325|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR304 crore, up 4.3% YoY, which management said was short of its guided growth because a shop-floor labour shortage in April to mid-June limited output, not demand. Auto components grew 13.5% to INR163 crore while bearing rings fell 6% to INR118 crore, with softness concentrated in domestic and European industrial bearing rings. EBITDA was INR69 crore at a 22.6% margin (up 100 bps YoY) and PAT rose 22% to INR60 crore, the third straight quarter of YoY margin expansion. Management said operations normalised from June, July 2026 was the highest-revenue month since inception, and it reiterated mid-teen FY27 revenue growth guidance while cutting its margin guidance to 21-22% citing ocean freight costs.

543330|2026-06.headline: Devyani Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore, with record Operating EBITDA of INR 151 crore (9.6% margin).
543330|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore and Operating EBITDA rose about 38% YoY to INR 151 crore, the company's highest ever, at a 9.6% margin. KFC returned to positive SSSG (3.3%) with dine-in salience improving to 57%, while Pizza Hut remained loss-making at brand contribution level with SSSG of -2.2%. Management flagged LPG, wage and commodity inflation, a weak monsoon outlook and volatile macro, and said Sapphire merger approvals from NSE and BSE were received in June with completion targeted by end FY27.

segments.commentary: Biryani By Kilo SSSG +7.2%, Vaango +7.1%; combined revenue INR 98 crore, gross margin 65.9%, brand contribution ~INR 10 crore (10.2%). 218 stores including 23 BBK Express; BBK target INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~6% YoY; gross margin fell to 74.6% on input costs; brand contribution margin 15.1%, up YoY on cost management.

qa_highlights.question: What drivers beyond SSSG could lift KFC margins from ~17% and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the key lever is ADS; crossing 105k-110k ADS should take KFC brand contribution above 20%. Other levers are dine-in promotion, operating leverage and technology adoption, which will only deliver a few quarters after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: Can KFC dine-in salience return to 60-65%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65% is not achievable near term given convenience preference, especially in the North; the target is 59-60%.

543331|2026-03.headline: Meghmani Organics FY26 standalone revenue rose 4% to INR 2,091 crore and EBITDA 27% to INR 228.7 crore, but Q4 standalone EBITDA was only INR 26.2 crore.
543331|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: US tariffs, a weaker export environment and the US-Iran war pushed raw material costs up while realisations stayed broadly flat. Standalone EBITDA recovered 27% for the full year, but Q4 remained thin, with Crop Protection margin near 9% and Pigments near 3%. Management suspended TiO2 operations as unviable after the anti-dumping duty was withdrawn and sulphuric acid prices spiked. Management guided to Crop Protection margins of 15-17% in FY27, double-digit Crop Protection top-line growth, and a Nano fertiliser ramp-up, and announced an amalgamation of two subsidiaries and a Brazil subsidiary.

segments.name: Pigments (FY26)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 461 crore (about 22% of revenue), EBITDA INR 15 crore, margin 3.3%; production about 13,191 MT at 40% utilisation. Q4 revenue INR 108 crore, EBITDA INR 3.2 crore, margin about 3%.

segments.commentary: Nano fertiliser products (Nano DAP, Nano NPK, Nano Zinc) received Ministry of Agriculture approval, to be made at Sanand, Gujarat with no additional capex. Commercial production expected in the Kharif season; Nano Urea is the key product, with about 7-8 products in the basket. No segment financials disclosed.

segments.commentary: Operations temporarily suspended as commercially unviable after the anti-dumping duty withdrawal, higher sulphuric acid and utility costs. Anti-dumping matter is under DGTR review.

qa_highlights.question: What growth rate should be expected and is the target on top line or bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years, with an internal aspiration of about 20%, for both top line and bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: How do the CPVC and PVC pricing respond to the recent MIP, and what is the outlook for CPVC demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MIP mainly hit carbide-based PVC, not the ethylene-based PVC Epigral uses, so no major impact is expected. CPVC realisation is about INR110-115/kg. Demand is expected to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality, though near-term overcapacity is likely as new capacity comes on.

qa_highlights.question: What are the chlorotoluenes and MPP capex, revenue and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore is done, with expected revenue of INR300-350 crore at optimum. Including MPP, the combined top line is targeted at INR700-800 crore, at an estimated margin of about 22-23%, with 1.5-2 years to optimum utilisation.

risks_watch: Epoxy and MPP margins will be lower than the 22-24% range, with ROCE of about 20% the stated offset; the margin trajectory of the combined business is not guided numerically.
CPVC overcapacity as Grasim and others add capacity, with utilisation at 50-55% in Q1 FY27 and a demand recovery expected only from Q3.
Caustic oversupply risk for a couple of years from domestic capacity additions, with utilisation at about 75% and ECU easing from INR35,000-36,000 to INR31,000-32,000/t.
ECH realisation fell from INR200-210/kg at the war-time peak to about INR180-185/t currently; ECH and glycerin prices are volatile, linked to crude, propylene and biodiesel policy.
Execution: the pilot facility is due by September 2026, ECH capacity doubling to 100,000 tpa and the 75,000 tpa CPVC expansion are due in a couple of months, and the MPP is targeted for FY28.
Leverage and returns: net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x from 0.6x, ROCE fell to 16% from 24%, and the INR600 crore project is 60% debt-funded.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28 keeps balance-sheet strain and the ROCE trajectory in focus.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 FY27 presented a highly challenging operating environment across all the segments, including chemicals.
Even against this volatile backdrop Epigral demonstrated a resilience, delivering a revenue growth of 15% and EBITDA margin of 25%.
So definitely, EBITDA margin in terms of percentage, definitely, it is coming lower.
Rather than giving guidance on margin, I can tell you that ROCE, we are targeting in the range of 20%.

543333|2026-03.headline: CarTrade Q4 FY26 PAT rose 54% YoY to INR70.8 crore; FY26 PAT INR243 crore (+68%), with management targeting INR1,000 crore profit in 4-5 years.

Consumer group (CarWale, BikeWale) grew revenue 25% in the quarter and 30% for the year. OLX India total income grew 16% in the quarter, below the ~18% of the prior quarter, which drew repeated analyst questions. Management pointed to new OLX monetisation products (Elite Buyer, Verification, Super Dost) as the next growth driver, but disclosed that these were still insignificant in revenue terms (under 5% of FY26 revenue).

segments.name: Remarketing (Shriram Automall)
segments.commentary: Revenue +22% in both FY26 and Q4; FY26 margin 28%, PAT +66%. Around 130 auction sites. Value-added and inspection fees are mostly auction-linked; inspection is under 10% of fees.

qa_highlights.question: What share of OLX revenue comes from Elite Buyer and Verification, and how big could it become in three years?

Management said the Surat grinding unit (2 mtpa) was inaugurated on 11 July 2026, ahead of schedule, and Kutch clinker and grinding remain on track for phased start from Q3 FY27. Management guided Q2 cost increase of about INR100 per ton, with power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton and packing and freight easing.

543336|2026-03.headline: Chemplast Q4 FY26 net loss of INR45 crores on INR898 crore CCVL impairment; consolidated EBITDA rose to INR194 crores from INR37 crores.

Management said suspension PVC spreads are at roughly breakeven on a replacement-cost basis because of Chinese carbide PVC imports, while specialty chemicals grew 13%. The Board also formed a committee of three independent directors to review strategic priorities, reorganisation and M&A.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

543349|2026-09.headline: Acutaas Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42.7% YoY to Rs 4,369 mn with EBITDA margin at 40.3%; FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to ~30%.
543349|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42.7% YoY to Rs 4,369 mn in Q2 FY27, driven by the Advanced Pharmaceutical Intermediate segment (Rs 4,020 mn, up 53.1%), while Specialty Chemicals fell 20% YoY to Rs 349 mn. Gross margin expanded 637 bps to 62.1% and EBITDA margin to 40.3% (up 914 bps), with PAT up 71.4% to Rs 1,231 mn. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 25% to about 30% and EBITDA margin guidance to 38-40%, and reaffirmed the CDMO target of Rs 1,000 mn... crores (Rs 1,000 crore) for FY27 and Rs 2,000 crore by FY30. Working capital days rose to 115 from 99 in Q1 on higher debtor days.

segments.name: Advanced Pharmaceutical Intermediates
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 4,020 mn in Q2 FY27, up 53.1% YoY; core pharma business grew more than 25% YoY. New CDMO contracts expected to contribute from H2 FY27. Management does not split CDMO from base business.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 349 mn, down 20% YoY due to phase-out of legacy commodity products and a temporary BFC shipment pause after a change in ownership of a U.S. customer; shipments have resumed.

segments.name: Battery Chemicals
segments.commentary: First quarter of commercial revenue. VC and FEC commercial supply started, third product dispatched in the quarter; fourth product at pilot-scale validation. Revenue not disclosed; ramp expected over next 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to around 30% from 25%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance raised to 38-40%; management confirmed this applies to FY27 only, not FY28.
CDMO revenue expected to cross Rs 1,000 crore in FY27, one year ahead of the FY28 target set in Jan 2025.
CDMO revenue target of Rs 2,000 crore by FY30; CDMO EBITDA margin expected in the same range as current CDMO margins.

Full-year FY27 capex about Rs 3,000 mn; H2 FY27 capex about Rs 1,650 mn (about Rs 1,000 mn electronic-grade chemicals, Rs 450 mn electrolyte additive phase 2, rest maintenance), excluding R&D capex and land acquisition.
Electronic-grade bulk chemicals plant expected to start production in H1 FY29.
Legacy Paraben and MS products to scale down over about 1-1.5 years; MS may take longer.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex Rs 1,239 mn across electrolyte additive project, pilot plant, Indicam site and maintenance.
Ankleshwar Unit 2 (CDMO): Rs 330 crore invested; utilisation 30% in Q2 FY27, expected to be no more than about 40% by end FY27; largely filled by FY28.
Indicam plant in South Korea inaugurated ahead of schedule; FY28 expected to be a ramp-up year for initial semiconductor products.
Next CDMO capex round deferred; land acquisition being planned first, with size to be decided later.
Battery chemicals plant utilisation described as very low at present.
demand_pricing: Pharma intermediate demand described as robust; cost pressures from geopolitical issues passed on to customers.
Several large generic products going off-patent; company has pre-developed intermediates for them.
Battery chemicals: industry demand exceeds supply; company cites strong order book.

Electrolyte additive pricing under long-term contracts linked to raw material and FX movements; management said realisations will be in the early teens (USD/kg basis implied) rather than the USD 30-35 spot levels cited by an analyst.
Management declined to say whether gross margin gain came from raw-material softening; said raw material prices had not softened in the quarter.
CDMO projects are all with originators, no generics; 8-10 products in pipeline; non-blockbuster products typically Rs 50-100 crore each.
Semiconductor customers targeted are in Korea, Japan and the U.S.; Indian ecosystem not yet mature.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from new CDMO products in FY27, and their contribution to the Rs 2,000 crore FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give product-wise revenue; FY27 Rs 1,000 crore CDMO target is backed by orders on already-validated products. Around 8-9 products to enter revenue over the next 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for battery, semiconductor and electronic-grade chemical revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery products already contributing; electronic-grade bulk chemical plant takes about 1.5 years to build, so production from H1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Electrolyte realisations versus recent price spike?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term supply contracts with raw material and FX-linked pricing; management says realisations can be early teens, not USD 30-35, and it does not chase price waves.

qa_highlights.question: Will Darolutamide volumes double from the same facility, and does Ankleshwar need capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is about 30% with room available; would not disclose wallet share or whether further capex is needed. It cannot comment on the product's market or indication expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Korea semiconductor facility: initial economics and target markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No tall commitment for FY28; revenue will be small initially with sample and pilot dispatches under way. Targets are photoresist and fab customers in Korea and Japan, not cell makers.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin guidance of 38-40% continue into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is for FY27 only; the margin uplift is attributed to CDMO mix and to operating leverage as Unit 2 and battery plants scale.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin expansion to 62.1%: how much is raw material versus mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot split the gain between raw material and mix; both contributed, and raw material prices did not soften in the quarter.

risks_watch: Specialty Chemicals revenue declined 20% YoY and remains a drag until legacy Paraben/MS exits and battery and BFC ramp up.
CDMO concentration: Darolutamide-linked volumes are a key driver, and management declined to discuss customer or product-level detail.
Working capital days rose to 115 from 99 in Q1 on higher debtor days.
Electronic-grade plant (H1 FY29) and Korea semiconductor ramp carry execution and qualification risk; management flagged geopolitical, supply chain, power and water constraints.
Margin guidance of 38-40% is for FY27 only; sustainability into FY28 is not guided.

543350|2026-03.headline: Vijaya Diagnostic Q4 FY26 revenue rose 26.6% YoY to INR 219 crore and EBITDA margin hit 43.5%, with FY27 margin guided at 40%+.
543350|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 26.6% YoY to INR 219 crore on 18.5% test volume growth, with the balance from test mix. EBITDA rose 38.7% to INR 95.5 crore (43.5% margin, up 379 bps), and PAT rose 37.5% to INR 47.9 crore. For FY26, revenue reached INR 814 crore (up 19.5%), EBITDA INR 337 crore (41.4% margin) and PAT INR 173 crore (21.2% margin). Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to "40%" while signalling it would aim higher, and planned 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes with INR 140-150 crore capex.

financial_highlights.change: Management attributed rise to new hub ramp-up mix

segments.name: Geography (Q4 revenue share)
segments.commentary: Hyderabad 67%, rest of AP/Telangana 20%, Pune (PH) 6%, West Bengal 4%, others 3%. Hyderabad grew ~20% YoY in Q4, a key driver of operating leverage.

segments.name: Pathology vs radiology
segments.commentary: Radiology was 37% of revenue; B2C was 92%. Both pathology and radiology drove growth.

segments.name: Pune (PH Diagnostics)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 16% YoY in Q4 (footfall ~15%), after Q3 growth of ~8%; Ambegaon hub reached breakeven in one year. Kalyani Nagar hub also opened in Q2 FY26.

segments.name: Wellness
segments.commentary: Growth consistently around 30%; packages roughly 50:50 radiology and pathology; average realisation INR 1,800-2,000 per patient, retail above INR 2,500.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: HSR and Yelahanka hubs (opened Q1 FY26): Yelahanka reached breakeven, HSR close to breakeven. Bannerghatta flagship with PET-CT, cardiac CT and wide-bore MRI expected ready in a couple of months.

segments.name: Kolkata / West Bengal
segments.commentary: 7 hubs in Kolkata; VIP Road grew double digits YoY; two Q1 FY26 hubs broke even in under 9 months; three newer centres (incl. Phoolbagan, Diamond Harbour) targeted for breakeven within a year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 40%+, with management saying it would be conservative and aim for better; company says it can deliver 30%+ even while opening new centres.

FY27 capex INR 140-150 crore for new centres and the automated lab; INR 120-130 crore for 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes from executed leases, plus automated lab in Panjagutta, Hyderabad; includes INR 10-12 crore replacement capex.
FY27 maintenance capex INR 10-15 crore, roughly 2-2.5% of topline.
Price hike of 1-1.5% planned, likely Q1 or Q2 FY27, on selected tests; realisation growth of 1-1.5% expected, with focus on volume growth over the next 2-3 years.
Pune expected to grow double digit in FY27 and to double revenue in 3-5 years; Hyderabad expected to grow double digit over 2-3 years.
Capex guidance to be revisited quarterly as new leases are executed; Bangalore, Pune, Kolkata or other geographies may add centres.
Genomics described as long-term play with no significant revenue in next few years; to be run from one central lab in Hyderabad.
capex_capacity: FY27 plan: 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes across network, with new fully automated lab at Panjagutta, Hyderabad with automated track system to improve turnaround time.

Network at call: ~50 hubs, ~112 spokes, 30 labs (including mini labs); 162 centres in total; ~95 in Hyderabad, ~35 in rest of AP/Telangana, 7 in Kolkata, 2 in Bangalore, 1 each in Gulbarga and Gurgaon, balance in Pune.
Two Pune hubs (Ambegaon and Kalyani Nagar) and two spokes opened recently; Pune capacity is a constraint in some PH centres, with existing-centre growth in low single digits.
Management is not pursuing North India for now; Gurgaon is a single wellness centre, and expansion focus is Karnataka and West Bengal for 3-5 years.
Inorganic: 8-15 assets come up each year; management will only add a large acquisition if it is B2C-driven, valuation-reasonable and of sufficient size.
demand_pricing: Hyderabad growth of ~20% in Q4 attributed to favourable season, market share gains and network expansion; management says it matches market rates, perhaps 2-3% higher.
Hospital-based labs compete; management says Vijaya is 20-25% cheaper than hospitals and differentiates on large format centres of 6,000-8,000 sq ft and integrated pathology and radiology.
Corporate wellness churn seen from price-sensitive corporates and aggregators; large corporate relationships continuing for 2-3 years; online players seen as having limited impact.
No GLP-1 (weight-loss drug) test-volume impact visible yet; requests for GLP packages not yet seen.

Management says revenue-per-test rise was driven by new hubs ramping up with radiology-heavy mix in first year; increase in wellness packages would raise revenue per patient but lower revenue per test.
Digital marketing spend of INR 6-7 crore in FY26 expected to double in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin outperformance in Q4 (43.5%) given other expenses grew 21%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base and new hubs breaking even faster than expected; Hyderabad growth of 20% helped. New-centre OPEX burn for FY26 was about 0.8% against the 2-2.5% envisaged. Incremental costs in talent and technology will continue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margin accretion be sharper given spoke-heavy additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margins may be similar to FY26 with 12 spokes and 4 hubs; more hubs would be a bigger drag. Guidance is 40%, with an aim to do better.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 280-300 crore cash be deployed, and what about M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will consider B2C-driven, same-ethos assets at reasonable valuations, with 8-15 opportunities a year. Capex guidance covers only executed leases and will be updated quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of the INR 150 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 120-130 crore for 4-5 hubs and 10-12 spokes from executed leases, plus the automated lab; includes INR 10-12 crore replacement capex.

qa_highlights.question: Pune hub ramp-up and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Both new Pune hubs have taken similar time; Ambegaon broke even in one year and Kalyani Nagar is expected to take a full year. Pune growth was slow after acquisition due to integration and culture work; management expects revenue to double in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Competition from hospital-based labs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hospital labs focus on in-patients and fasting OPD tests, and Vijaya's 20-25% lower prices and integrated large-format centres differentiate it; Bangalore has no large integrated player.

risks_watch: FY27 margin could compress if more hubs (versus spokes) open, since new hubs carry higher ramp-up costs; management said the 40% guide is conservative.
Pune growth is still low-to-mid-teens and depends on capacity additions and the corporate segment; management has previously missed its Pune targets.
Corporate wellness churn from price-sensitive clients and aggregators; wellness repeat-customer data has only been tracked for about two years.
Genomics and AI investments are early; AI tools need regulatory validation, and CRM/ERP rollouts are due in FY27 after an earlier LIMS hiccup.
Quarterly updates on capex and centre count promised; watch for executed leases and any large M&A deal.

543350|2026-06.headline: Vijaya Diagnostic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to ~Rs 231 crore and EBITDA margin hit 42.7%, up 360 bps.

EBITDA rose 34% to Rs 98 crore (42.7% margin) and PAT rose 37.6% to Rs 53 crore (23% margin). The company reiterated a capex plan of Rs 190-195 crore for 9 hubs, 10-12 spokes and a Panjagutta reference lab, and guided to high double-digit growth for FY27.

segments.name: Pune (PH)
segments.commentary: Contributed 6% of revenue and grew ~18% YoY, from ~Rs 10.8 crore to ~Rs 12.8 crore; management expects growth to continue with 2 more hubs in 12 months.

segments.name: West Bengal
segments.commentary: Contributed 4% of revenue; Krishna Nagar hub reached breakeven in about 2 quarters.

segments.name: Mature centres vs new centres
segments.commentary: Mature centres grew 16%; new centres contributed 6-6.5% of revenue. Burn from hubs not yet at breakeven is ~0.5% of top line, under Rs 1 crore EBITDA loss in the quarter.

segments.name: Radiology and pathology
segments.commentary: Both grew; B2C was 92% of revenue and radiology 37% of revenue per the call.

543358|2026-06.headline: Sansera Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR10,213 million, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and ADS order book lifted to about INR57.5 billion.

FY26 revenue reached INR9,550.7 million (+25.6%) and PAT INR1,718 million (+44.6%), with a net cash position of INR2,437.1 million. qa_highlights.question: Was the 1.5x to 2x FY27 outperformance guidance a downgrade from 2x to 2.5x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. The 2.5x in FY26 was specific to large export wins and the Hero program; 1.5x to 2x has been the consistent guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Walter Pack shed low-margin products, a new higher-value program is in ramp-up, and some Q3 orders were pulled forward to beat tariff uncertainty. Management expects growth to return over the next one to two quarters.

Consolidated operating revenue grew 40% to ₹1,888 Cr, core insurance revenue rose 46% and core credit revenue rose 25%, while PAT margin improved from 6% to 9%. Management repeatedly stated that growth, not margin expansion, remains the priority, with acquisition spend being increased. Management also said Q1 is seasonally weak and flagged that the GST-related health and term demand tailwind is already fading.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating expenses excluding contribution, % of revenue

segments.name: Insurance (Policybazaar)
segments.commentary: Core new insurance premium incl. savings grew 39%, excluding savings 48%. New health grew 59% and new health and term grew 53%. Management says 82% of business is from customers new to insurance.

segments.name: Credit (Paisabazaar)
segments.commentary: Core revenue grew 25% and core disbursals 33%, with total disbursals at ₹4,366 Cr. Operating EBITDA broke even in Q1 and contribution margin was 41%; management expects FY27 EBITDA about half of the ~₹100 Cr previously discussed.

segments.name: PB Partners (POSP)
segments.commentary: Active partners rose 55% YoY to 1.13 lakh and 78% of GWP comes from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Top 100 partners account for 16% of premium; POSP premium is about ₹1,600 Cr and corporate about ₹500 Cr.

segments.name: UAE / Dubai
segments.commentary: UAE insurance premium grew 31% YoY, about ₹500 Cr in the quarter, mainly health and life.

segments.name: PB Health
segments.commentary: Quarterly loss about ₹7 Cr. Second hospital got billing approval; internal target is ~₹500 Cr annual run rate and break-even by March 2027.

segments.name: PB Connect
segments.commentary: Revenue about ₹12 Cr from retail. Wholesale consolidation business was discontinued, so the line is down 73% YoY and was zero from wholesale in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects renewal growth to exceed fresh growth over the next 12 months, with renewal growth upwards of 50% for some time.
Management says long-term target of about 30% growth remains; margin efficiency is deferred in favour of growth, with efficiency expected later.
Management says the GST-driven insurance demand tailwind is fading in Q1 and it may be lucky if it persists in Q2.
PB Health targets ~₹500 Cr annual run rate and break-even by March 2027.
Paisabazaar FY27 EBITDA expected at roughly half of the previously discussed ~₹100 Cr; Q1 at break-even.
Several launches planned for end-August 2026, including bonds via PB Money entity and daily SIP platform on Paisabazaar.
capex_capacity: Hiring: about 5,000 gross hires in Q1 FY27 despite seasonal weakness.
Call-centre talk time for health transactions reduced from about 2 hours at IPO to 35-40 minutes now.
AI touches 30-40% of about 10 crore monthly customer interactions; 20-30% of service interactions are automated.
Second PB Health hospital received billing approval; more hospitals in pipeline.
demand_pricing: Health and term growth is attributed to demand creation spend, product features like monthly mode (over 30% of health business) and a 3-month maternity waiting period, and claims service (CSAT above 90%, ~70,000 health claims supported in the quarter).
Tier 2 and Tier 3 account for 65-70% of direct online business and are growing faster than metros; South has grown faster than North and West over three years.
Motor plus two-wheeler direct grew over 30%; motor POSP grew close to 50%. Retail direct TP is about 25% of premium value; POSP motor is about half TP.
Waiver of Premium (WOP) share in domestic savings has crossed 60% in some centres in July; savings fresh business grew over 20%.
Management views the Supreme Court TP-extension judgement as a potential upside via enforcement, but says it is too early to quantify.
Management said Q3 FY26 was an above-trend quarter, making the H2 base high, and said the goal is above-market growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where is health and term growth coming from (Tier 2/3 vs urban) and is the user base different from peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed outgrowth to demand investment, relevant tailored products, and claims service; 82% of business is from customers without prior insurance, and port-in is a small share.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve as renewals grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renewal growth will beat fresh growth for ~12 months but will keep reinvesting in acquisition for lifetime value; margin improvement is secondary to fresh growth.

qa_highlights.question: Regulatory commission changes and the worst-case manufacturer scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not anticipate changes, pointed to legal effort requirements on brokers, and said insurance requires heavy enquiry and conversion spend, with platform cost the smallest part.

qa_highlights.question: Paisabazaar EBITDA and Tier 2/3 mix in online business?
qa_highlights.answer: Paisabazaar broke even on an operating basis in Q1 and is expected to be about half of the earlier ~₹100 Cr full-year number. Tier 2 and Tier 3 are 65-70% of direct business.

qa_highlights.question: Dark patterns and H2 growth base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denies deception in phone-number collection and said Q3 FY26 was above trend; aims to keep above-market growth. On AI, management said productivity gains may mean hiring less for the same business, while growth remains the goal.

qa_highlights.question: Expense ratio decline and call-centre cost classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Expenses excluding contribution fell to 58% of revenue from 61%; management said costs grew about 35% against 40% revenue growth and that efficiency drives have not started. All call-centre employee costs sit in employee benefit expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Savings business softness and reputation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says fresh savings grew over 20% and persistency is about 100 bps below its best; it said ULIPs are sold through verification calls and are low-cost.

PB Health: Q1 loss about ₹7 Cr; target of ~₹500 Cr annual run rate and break-even by March 2027, described as an internal target that may be missed.
Motor TP: Supreme Court judgment on TP extension and enforcement could be upside, but management says it is too early to quantify; PB Connect wholesale exit reduces that line by 73% YoY.
key_quotes: And you're consistently hearing the same thing from management across the board, that our P1 is growth, efficiency will come, it'll be for later.
Right now, we are in the middle of this GST thing. We saw Q3, very big; Q4, big. Now in Q1, it has already started to fade, and I think we'll be lucky if it goes through in Q2.
So all I'm explaining is we haven't started efficiency yet. That will come at some point, but it's not time for that yet.
