543396|2026-03.headline: Paytm Q4 FY26: management expects revenue growth to accelerate in FY27 and EBITDA margin to reach 15-20% in two and a half to three years, with no quantified Q4 margin figures in transcript.
543396|2026-03.overview: Management said payments (about 55% of revenue) and marketing services (about 30%) are the main tailwinds for FY27 acceleration, with personal loans recovering and wealth as a new growth leg. Postpaid disbursal ramp is described as faster than the earlier launch, though no figures were given and management declined to comment on guidance. Net payment margin was about 9 bps, with management pointing to pricing discipline and credit instruments on UPI as drivers. Management said it will spend more on cashback and customer acquisition but within existing guidance, and that new investment will go only into AI, with no material capex plan yet. The company is not pursuing an NBFC licence and says the wallet licence remains a commitment without a timeline.

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: About 55% of revenue; benefiting from offline and UPI credit tailwinds, full payment licence now in place, and rising MDR-bearing instrument mix. Management said MDR-bearing mix growth is lifting net payment margin.

segments.name: Marketing services
segments.commentary: About 30% of revenue; management expects it to contribute to FY27 growth after a drag from a revamp and a headwind in advertising, with management citing a lower base.

segments.name: Financial services (lending distribution)
segments.commentary: Paytm acts as a distribution channel and does not own the loan book; personal loan disbursements recovered in the latest month. Management said wealth/broking is a third leg with low market share, and that retail broking and wealth are targeted for a top-five position.

segments.name: Consumer and merchant sides
segments.commentary: Management said consumer-side and merchant-side profitability was the best in eight quarters. Online merchant GMV is growing and is described as a double-digit share of GMV, not single digit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth to accelerate in FY27, with payments and marketing services as the main contributors.
Management expects to reach 15-20% EBITDA margin in two and a half to three years; the analyst's question on the timing received no firm quantified answer.
Management expects significant operating leverage going forward, but declined to give quarter-on-quarter detail.
Cashback and customer-acquisition spend will rise in absolute terms but is said to remain within previously given guidance.
Management said next year's capex will be higher than current levels; this was noted by the analyst as a cash-flow item.
Management said it expects near-full offset of the PIDF subsidy sunset on subscription revenue per device, after achieving a 30-40% offset target in Q4.
capex_capacity: Management said there is no material capex plan yet for AI; any new investment will go only into AI, with the approach of renting data centre capacity and GPUs rather than building.
Management said the company expects capex to rise next year, but gave no figure.
Device base is growing: about 27 lakh devices added, per analyst, with capex per device said to be lower; cohort payback periods are improving.
demand_pricing: Credit-card-on-UPI share of volume is small; management says this share is higher than for standard bank accounts, and Paytm sees no moderation in its own GMV growth.
EMI enablement covers more than half of machines; EMI is used across electronics, healthcare, furniture, fashion, beauty and quick commerce, with a Rs 5,000+ ticket size.
Agentic checkout funnel conversion was described as about 7-8 times higher than the tap-based funnel, per management.
Management said the NBFC licence is not a priority; it prefers the distribution model with multiple lender balance sheets.
Penetration of lending in the merchant base is about 7%, rising about 1% a year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said traction is better than before and that personal loan disbursements started to recover in the latest month. It gave no figures and declined to comment on guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of net payment margin upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited pricing discipline and the shift to credit instruments on UPI rails, with postpaid starting to contribute; it said a small share of GMV can add 20-40 bps.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarter-on-quarter changes include appraisal impact; AI-driven efficiencies and an expected acceleration should produce operating leverage. It declined to say whether the path is front- or back-ended.

543396|2026-06.headline: Paytm Q1 FY27: management reports broad-based growth acceleration, with GMV up 31% YoY and EBITDA margin at about 8%, targeting a 15-20% medium-term margin.
543396|2026-06.overview: Management said growth accelerated across all payment businesses, with GMV up 31% YoY (versus 23% in Q3 and 27% in Q4 as cited by an analyst) and sales and services revenue up 27% YoY. Adjusted for PIDF, the net payment margin moved from 8.4% to 8.8% (figures as discussed on the call), and management said the EBITDA margin is about 8% this quarter. Employee costs fell about 6.5% YoY excluding sales costs, which management attributed to AI-led efficiency and flat headcount rather than a one-off. Management framed the 15-20% margin as a medium-term direction, not a number to guide to, and said cash on the balance sheet was built up from INR 13,500 crore a year ago.

financial_highlights.change: Accelerated from about 27% in Q4 per analyst; management said acceleration is seen in every payments business
Adjusted for PIDF, growth of about 8% per management's commentary
Management cited a ~9 pp YoY improvement as discussed by an analyst
Rising gradually each quarter; analyst noted 10.6 to 11.2 bps increase in processing costs
Despite appraisals; management said no one-off and ESOP accounted for

financial_highlights.value: Management cited growth from INR 13,500 crore a year ago
financial_highlights.change: Balance sheet cash described as growing with strong free cash flow
Management expects roughly linear growth from here

segments.commentary: Management said most profit comes from the merchant side, with growth accelerating; merchant loans are now a double-digit lending partner base. Management said offline is a strength.

segments.name: Consumer / P2P and UPI
segments.commentary: Management said P2P is not lower margin than P2M, and that monthly active users grew 8% YoY with GTV up 45%. Postpaid is still under INR 1,000 crore a month in usage.

segments.name: Financial services (lending, MTF, broking, MF distribution)
segments.commentary: Management said credit is distribution-led with no FLDG, partners' capital deployed is 4-6x Paytm's, and MTF is an ROI use of excess cash. Wealth/broking was described as a bright spot but still small.

segments.name: Marketing services
segments.commentary: Management said growth is behind merchant but not far behind, with travel as a headwind due to higher airfares and leisure demand.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a numeric long-term EBITDA margin; directionally, it cited 15-16% as a terminal figure in one answer and 15-20% as the medium-term target.
Management expects 25-30 lakh lending additions a year, with the pace continuing.
Management expects continued profitability improvement, with investment in sales and marketing ongoing.
Management said the postpaid book could reach the INR 9,000 crore peak earlier, at about twice the earlier pace.
capex_capacity: Management said AI models were tuned in-house (a 4 billion parameter Indian-language model), running on Paytm's own infrastructure to cut compute costs.
No capacity or capex figures were given on the call.
demand_pricing: Management said GMV growth is broad-based across categories and not concentrated in a few businesses.
Management said Rupay credit on UPI continues to rise as a share of mix.
Management said fintech partners are seeing a desire to lend unsecured, with healthy bureau profiles.
Management said UPI MDR changes would have no material impact on Paytm, as merchants and enterprises paying or not paying MDR both benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins reach 20% long term, and what drives the margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not giving a number now and that margin is a trade-off with investment, but that the 15-20% range is structural. Drivers cited were operating leverage, AI-led efficiency and better unit economics.

qa_highlights.question: Is GMV acceleration sustainable and what is driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said acceleration is seen in every payments business, with offline and online growing at different rates. It said the growth is sustainable, with offline digitisation and the customer base as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the government's UPI MDR change matter for Paytm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no visibility on the formula and is modelling it internally. It said there is no material impact, since merchants paying or not paying MDR benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why are merchant subscription revenues being reduced on some plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a deliberate decision to discount subscription rentals for merchants with material revenue, to drive sign-ups, and that a tighter revenue recognition policy was applied on certain businesses.

qa_highlights.question: How much did employee costs fall, and is that sustainable?

543396|2026-09.headline: Paytm's Q2 FY27: two quarters of 28% growth; 2.5 bps UPI MDR could add about ₹700 crore EBITDA at current GMV.
543396|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with reported growth of 28% for two consecutive quarters and about 30%+ excluding the prior-year PIDF effect. Payments GMV was roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to seasonality (late Diwali) and to walking away from unprofitable large merchant contracts. The call centred on the UPI MDR framework (which was postponed from 15 October to post-Diwali), the AI-led merchant platform, and the DLG accounting change with one lending partner. Management said MDR is upside to the model and not factored into its base plan. Cloud/AI costs rose, with management attributing the increase to a one-time consolidation of online and offline payment stacks plus ongoing AI spend.

financial_highlights.change: Up, per analyst framing; management attributed to pricing discipline and share gains

segments.commentary: Management said lending is growing well across the board and that personal loans are in a tailwind. segments.commentary: Management said the marketing services business has recovered and that AI-driven merchant service revenue will be booked in marketing services. Management guided that this would take two to three more quarters to become meaningful.

543399|2026-03.headline: Tarsons Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7.3% to INR120.9 crore, but margins compressed on raw material spikes and new-plant costs; FY27 PAT guided moderate.
543399|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with standalone revenue up 4.4% YoY to about INR97 crore and domestic growth of 11.7% offsetting a 13.4% decline in exports tied to Middle East disruptions. Gross margin fell to 58.5% standalone in Q4 as raw material prices spiked from mid-March, and EBITDA was pressured by commissioning costs at the Amta and Panchla plants. Management said the large capex programme is nearly complete, with full commissioning expected in H1 FY27, and that no major new capex is planned beyond about INR20 crore of maintenance spend. Management guided FY27 PAT to remain at a moderate level, with operating leverage expected to improve from FY27.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 exports fell 13.4% YoY on Middle East supply-chain disruption, container shortages and freight costs; FY26 exports grew about 3%. Management said some supply-chain easing was seen in the last two weeks and enquiries are reviving.

segments.commentary: Bioprocess bottles ramping well; several cell culture lines commercially launched over the last 2-3 months, with pilot production on some lines and more starting in the next quarter. Management expects meaningful scale-up from FY28.

Standalone depreciation for FY27 guided at about INR105-110 crore, the peak level, as INR158 crore of CWIP moves into fixed assets.
No major capex planned for FY27-28; maintenance and small commercial capex of about INR20 crore in FY27.
FY27 PAT expected at a relatively moderate level, with accounting losses not expected; PAT guided to single-digit percentage with PBT of about 9-10%.
Q1 FY27 gross margin should not fall below 65%, per the CFO, and management said Q1 margins should be in a similar region to Q4.
Net debt target: debt not to exceed 2x EBITDA; free cash flow to be used mainly for deleveraging over the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Large-scale capex programme begun about four years ago is in its final phase; bioprocess lines, liquid handling capacity and selected cell culture lines already commissioned.
INR158 crore of CWIP still on the balance sheet, to be capitalised in FY27 and adding depreciation.
Amta and Panchla facilities carried high commissioning and operating costs in FY26 that management expects to stabilise as utilisation ramps up.

Management said it expects to serve Nerbe (consolidated subsidiary) with products from India after capacity expansion, where financially viable.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices rose about 60-70% from normalised levels since mid-March, driven by Middle East and Asian supply disruption; raw material supply is also constrained across the industry.
Management began gradual, product-by-product price increases from April FY27 but said full pass-through is not feasible given price-list cycles and competition from imports and MNC inventory.
Chinese competition in the US and Europe described as fierce; India-EU FTA, if effective, could provide a few percentage points of duty advantage versus China.
Management says exports face US buyer pressure on pricing and that the rupee depreciation is a cost advantage only on local components, with raw materials still imported.
Industry domestic demand declined about 8% YoY while Tarsons grew 4.5% YoY; Q4 Tarsons grew about 16% QoQ versus industry 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation outlook and capex for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation is on written-down value (18% machinery and moulds, 10% buildings). Standalone FY27 depreciation is guided at INR105-110 crore, with no major capex beyond about INR20 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Will export growth be strong in FY27 now that US tariffs have eased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit; raw material spikes have made Indian producers less competitive versus US manufacturers, and stronger growth needs normalised conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 FY27 margins be worse than Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins should be in a similar range to Q4, not worse; the CFO said gross margin should not fall below 65%, against about 68% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will free cash flow go to deleveraging?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; the focus over 2-3 years is deleveraging, with debt ideally kept below 2x EBITDA. Fundraising could be considered only if a significant opportunity arises.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pass through the full raw material increase to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price-book cycles (generally annual), competitors absorbing short-term price spikes, and large existing import inventory that could enable price undercutting.

Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation, freight and container availability, and US and Europe competition from China.

Higher depreciation (INR105-110 crore FY27) and interest keep PAT thin, with FY27 PAT guided to moderate levels.

543399|2026-06.headline: Tarsons Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR 110.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23.6% on input-cost spikes of 25-50%.
543399|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR 110.2 crore and standalone revenue reached INR 86.1 crore, the company's highest Q1 standalone revenue. Domestic sales grew 17% and exports rose about 29%, with the German subsidiary Nerbe up about 6% in constant currency. Gross margin (standalone) fell to 67.1% on polymer price spikes, and consolidated EBITDA was INR 26 crore (23.6% margin), with new-facility operating costs also weighing. Management said the remaining Panchla lines are due for full commissioning in Q2, with revenue contribution from H2 FY27, and that FY27 profit will stay moderate.

segments.name: Exports (India)
segments.commentary: Grew about 29% YoY after disruption from West Asia tensions and US tariffs; international price increases were close to zero, with reliance on rupee depreciation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the sheer number of machines and lines, supplier and engineering issues; a few months' delay on remaining lines. Q1 Panchla revenue came from existing products or capacity shifted there, with bioprocess containers and roller bottles contributing.

qa_highlights.question: What are gross and net debt, and will interest and depreciation peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR 380 crore, net debt about INR 330-340 crore. FY27 depreciation INR 105-110 crore is the peak. Interest run rate ~INR 20 crore per year, to fall in FY28. Debt reduction about INR 40 crore YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is left and what peak revenue can it support?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 160 crore CWIP and INR 20 crore capital advances to complete within Q2-Q3 FY27, no new major capex. Peak incremental revenue estimated at INR 750-800 crore on ~0.8x asset turnover.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken and what is the outlook for gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes are marginal and mostly domestic; international pricing close to zero. Management could not call the margin bottom given volatile raw material costs and said erosion is external rather than operational.

qa_highlights.question: What will it take to grow beyond 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees 20-22% as doable with new products, cell culture and export support; 15% is the base case including white labelling and contract manufacturing for export.

qa_highlights.answer: Panchla and Amta are expected to contribute 20-25% of standalone revenue in FY28; new product portfolio revenue INR 65-70 crore in FY28. Maintenance capex no more than INR 20-25 crore a year.

543401|2026-03.headline: Go Fashion Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR196 crore with EBITDA margin at 25.3%; management guides FY27 SSSG positive and margin recovery from Q2.
543401|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR196 crore, gross margin 62.9%, EBITDA INR50 crore (25.3% margin) and PAT INR8 crore, with FY26 revenue at INR838 crore and PAT at INR59 crore. Full-year FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin was 11.5% versus 16.8% in FY25, with EBITDA down about INR40 crore to INR96 crore. Management is closing small EBOs (50-plus in FY26, about 50 more in Q1 FY27) and shifting to 700-plus sq ft stores, while the LFS channel recovered from about minus 30% in Q3 to about minus 7% in Q4 after adjusting for a INR5 crore credit note. Same-store sales growth was negative for FY26 and management targets positive SSSG by end FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Reported SSSG is based on stores live through the year; about 275 stores were SSSG-positive in Q4 at roughly 10-11% average, mostly 300+ sq ft stores. Management said about 200-210 of the positive stores are above 300 sq ft.

NEP growth is expected to lag GWP growth because of long-term policy sales, with catch-up expected in coming quarters.
Management expects the long-term share of NEP to keep rising next year.
Agent network to reach 1 million in two years, adding about 1 lakh agents a year.
capex_capacity: Home Healthcare, telemedicine and condition management usage rose 4-5x over the year, with Q4 consumption up about 9x. FY26 included over 90,000 telemedicine calls and over 40,000 pure telemedicine calls.
Claims platform migration to the Medi Assist platform is nearly complete, with the last product set to shift by Q1 FY27 end.
Customer app has over 14 million downloads and more than 1.5 million monthly active users; 95% of fresh premium is collected digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail Health premiums grew 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26 versus 11.2% for non-life. For full FY26, retail health grew close to 20% and non-life 9.3%.
New-to-insurance share of fresh premium was 94% in Q4 (90% a year earlier) and 93% for FY26 (89% in FY25).
Volume retention improved 1-1.5% YoY; the company cited about 86-87% volume retention and a renewal ratio of 99%. GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps and NOP-based 100 bps.
Agent productivity rose about 37% on fresh and 18% on total business. Over 90% of retail comes from agency and D2C channels.
Senior citizens are about 20% of the portfolio; the senior citizen commission reduction took effect April 2024 (FY25) and drove part of the commission ratio gain.
Long-term vs annual NEP split is about 80:20, moving 100-150 bps toward long-term on premium basis.

qa_highlights.question: How will the retail loss ratio (about 68%) get back to 65-66% levels seen in FY23-24, and how will seasonal vector-borne claims be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said frequency and severity were managed in the high-single digits for FY26 and that Q4 benefited from lower frequency. It cited telemedicine and home healthcare usage growth and repricing of about 80% of the book from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27, but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail growth lagging the industry, and how should the gap evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises quality and profitable geographies over market share. Its market share was 31.3% in FY26, growth on N basis was 39% for FY26, and the company is not chasing share at the cost of profit.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the loss ratio improvement: renewal book, new business, severity or fraud controls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain is a sum of parts: renewal repricing, sourcing quality, geography selection, and fraud, waste and abuse controls. Q4 frequency improvement cut across the whole book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the retention ratio uptick linked to long-term policies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the Q3/Q4 retention noise to renewals pulled into September after the GST cut, with some spillover into Q1. Volume retention improved 1-1.5% for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for a major repricing in FY27, and is the current price rise enough for the target combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no need for above-normal increases. It expects the current annual pricing strategy to be sufficient to hit the target combined ratio.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bima Sugam expected to affect sourcing and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bima Sugam is a consumer platform for affordable plans, that it will not be zero-cost, and that Star Health is a shareholder and supportive of it.

qa_highlights.question: Did the GST cut lift renewals and sum insured?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Walia said GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps, with customers opting for higher sum insured and riders, and that distributor income had risen over 50% since the GST announcement.

qa_highlights.question: Management did not answer on the EoM regulation's treatment of non-compliant companies and declined to comment on it, saying IRDAI guidance on EoM is awaited.

risks_watch: Retail loss ratio is still about 68% for FY26 versus the 65-66% seen in FY23-24; sustainability of the Q4 frequency improvement across a full cycle is unproven.

543412|2026-06.headline: Star Health Q1 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 111 crore from Rs 16 crore, with CISR improving to 97% and normalised PAT up 44% to Rs 386 crore.
543412|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed a fourth successive quarter of improving core underwriting profitability, with underwriting result at Rs 111 crore versus Rs 16 crore a year earlier. Reported PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 550 crore, while normalised PAT (8% investment yield basis) rose 44% to Rs 386 crore, giving annualised ROE of 15.6% versus 12.2%. Fresh retail GWP grew 37% YoY to Rs 730 crore on a 1/N basis, but retail market share slipped to 29% from 31%, which management attributed to long-term policy accounting and deliberate avoidance of riskier pools. Management guided insurance revenue growth to rise towards 15-16% and expense ratio to fall 30-40 bps a year, while declining to give loss ratio guidance.

segments.name: Retail health
segments.commentary: Retail market share 29% vs 31% a year earlier; new-to-insurance mix in fresh retail 94% vs 90%. Proprietary channels (agency and D2C) are 90%+ of retail business.

segments.name: Group health
segments.commentary: Group share of GWP is now roughly 2.5%, down from about 5% a year earlier; management said group contributed part of the loss ratio improvement but retail also improved.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C fresh business grew 142% YoY, with 98% of customers new to insurance; D2C is 74% of digital fresh business.

guidance_outlook: Insurance revenue growth is expected to rise from 13.4% towards 15-16% as the quarters progress, and to increase further in FY28.
Expense ratio expected to improve 30-40 bps consistently each year from technology and productivity investments.

Reinsurance cost expected to fall: the voluntary quota share treaty (2023-24 and 2024-25, three-year) is fading out, and obligatory treaty renegotiation with GICRE may bring benefits; FY28 net reinsurance benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%.
Q2 is seasonally higher for loss ratio; management expects the same trend this year. No loss ratio guidance given.
Steady-state ROE target is mid-to-high teens on an Ind AS basis; no specific number given.
Fresh-business growth expected to moderate in H2 FY27 and into H1 FY28 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds; management agreed this framing.
capex_capacity: Agency network added about 20,000 agents in the quarter to 8.5 lakh; agent productivity up 19% YoY.
Non-metro fresh business growth is 3.5x metro growth.
Customer app has about 16 million downloads and 1.5 million+ monthly active users.
97% of new applications are digitally sourced; generative AI being layered on existing AI/ML claims analytics.
Long-term policies are about 40% of retail fresh business; fresh-to-renewal share about 20:80 in insurance revenue.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is partly driven by the GST waiver; majority of fresh business comes from first-time buyers. Management expects moderation of optical growth rates.

Pricing is annual and product-by-product on a calendar; most pricing actions have been taken in Q4 over the last couple of years, with earned impact flowing through subsequent quarters. Management described upcoming pricing as maintenance-level rather than step-up, with some discounts for non-claimants.
Retail claim settlement ratio 91%; over 9.5 lakh claims settled in the quarter, over 80% cashless.
Senior citizens are under 5% of the book; focus remains on younger cohorts.
Management is watching dengue, malaria and fever outbreaks; telemedicine and home healthcare used to manage these cases.

qa_highlights.question: How will GWP growth of 19% convert into insurance revenue growth, and when will they converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance revenue grew 13.4%; management expects 15-16% through the year as long-term policy earnings build, and higher growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers for loss ratio improvement and how many claims are settled via telemedicine?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combined approach: repricing, portfolio selection, claims fraud control, network management, wellness and teleconsultation. No telemedicine claim count was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the expense ratio improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects 30-40 bps annual expense ratio improvement from tech, digitisation and productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of acquisition cost is employee expense and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is split three ways: claims-related in claims, sales-related in acquisition cost, and support costs in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinsurance impact on the expense ratio and what is the full-year benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Reinsurance cost is falling as the quota share treaty fades; FY28 benefit guided at roughly 0.5-0.6%, though management said this was hard to pin down.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow in H2 as the GST-driven base builds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that H2 FY27 and early FY28 growth could be lower on the high base, and said it will not chase growth for its own sake.

risks_watch: Seasonal Q2 loss ratio pressure from vector-borne and infectious diseases.
Regulatory changes to commissions and claims reforms; management declined to comment until rules are final.

Fresh growth may moderate in H2 FY27 as the post-GST-waiver base effect builds.

543412|2026-09.headline: Star Health Q2 FY27 underwriting profit rose to Rs 99 crore from a Rs 40 crore loss, with PAT up over threefold to Rs 265 crore.
543412|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 marked the fifth successive quarter of improving loss ratios and underwriting results, with CISR improving 2.9 points to 98%. Gross written premium on a reported 1/n basis grew 19% YoY to Rs 5,275 crore in Q2 and Rs 9,562 crore in H1, while fresh retail health GWP grew 35% in the quarter. Normalized PAT (at an 8% investment yield) rose 70% YoY to Rs 390 crore in Q2. Management flagged that headline growth will moderate in H2 as last year's GST-led surge enters the base, and that regulatory proposals on distribution commissions and expense of management (EoM) are the next key uncertainty.

segments.name: Retail health (fresh)
segments.commentary: Fresh retail GWP grew 35% YoY in Q2 and 36% in H1 on reported 1/n basis; new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% from 89%, with new-to-insurance policies up over 10% and average sum insured up 13%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Network reached 8.7 lakh agents after adding 39,000 in H1; agency productivity up 19% YoY; agency contributes about 70-75% of fresh business and grew about 25% in Q2 per management.

segments.name: Digital D2C
segments.commentary: D2C grew 137% YoY in H1 and its share of business rose from 8% to 13%; management says D2C has superior combined ratios. Proprietary channels (agency plus D2C) account for over 90% of retail business.

segments.name: Renewal book
segments.commentary: Management says the standalone renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio; vintage book is about 80% of portfolio. Group business is now a very small share of premium.

guidance_outlook: Company aspires to grow fresh business at 20%+ consistently over a long period and hopes to maintain that for FY27, though optical growth moderation is expected in Q3 and Q4 due to GST-led base.
ROE ambition to move from mid-teens to higher-teens over time, with combined ratio as the key lever.
Retail market share and like-for-like comparability under 1/n reporting expected to be restored only by FY28.
Management believes it has a credible path to the proposed EoM limits through operating leverage, productivity and digitization, but will give more detail once regulation is final.
Company will not disclose point-to-point guidance on individual loss ratio metrics.
capex_capacity: Equity allocation about 14% (slightly less than 14%), with internal strategy to cap at around 15%; management may go beyond 15% if markets are very attractive.

Portfolio duration increased toward a target of about 4 years after G-Sec yields rose; management said it has taken some long-duration G-Sec calls and may extend duration further if yields keep rising.
REITs and InvITs: fully invested against the 3% regulatory limit with a small margin of safety; AIF allocation about 2.1-2.2% of funds and growing slowly.
Digital SBU created last year; Salesforce CRM upgraded; AI bots processed over 7.5 million minutes of call volume at under 20% of human cost.
demand_pricing: Fresh growth is driven by a mix of price, volume and higher average sum insured; management did not split the contribution.
Around 80% of the book was repriced in the last cycle; the remaining portion is being repriced this year, with further correction as needed based on loss ratios.
Packages account for about 80% of claims; hospital negotiations described as business as usual, with the Supreme Court drug-pricing order not yet notified.
Management estimates a fresh-to-insurance market share near 40% (not a reported figure) and notes the reported fresh figure includes portability.
Commission ratio moderated YoY because the senior citizen commission cut (15% to 10%) and other efficiencies now show a full 12-month impact.

qa_highlights.question: How is fresh growth tracking in October and by channel, now that the GST-led base is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects optical moderation in Q3 and Q4 but aims for 20%+ fresh growth; it tracks policies sold, agent activations and digital activations.

qa_highlights.question: Is the loss ratio improvement driven by fresh business or by the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Improvement is driven by the vintage book (about 80% of portfolio), since the fresh book at about 20% of the portfolio could not drive it alone; renewal book now operates below 100% combined ratio. Fresh and renewal loss ratios are not disclosed separately.

qa_highlights.question: Loss ratio decomposition in Q2 (frequency, severity, pricing) and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss cost held at mid-single-digit growth while earned premium grew close to double digits; management did not give point-to-point metric guidance and will focus on combined ratio going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Equity and duration positioning, and whether there is an equity cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity about 14%, no incremental purchases this quarter; the 15% level is an internal strategy, not a formal cap. Duration lengthened toward about 4 years via G-Sec calls.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company responding to the Rs 59 crore investment-related loss and its FVTPL classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity, ETFs, REITs and InvITs are classified as FVTPL; debt is held to maturity. No breakdown of the Rs 59 crore between realized and unrealized was provided in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the insurance finance income and expense restatement, and will it stay nil?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance finance income and expense (significant financing component on long-term policies) was discontinued as an optional treatment; it is now nil and has no PAT impact because the offsetting income sits in restated insurance revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How are multi-year policies commissioned, and what is the impact of the proposed distribution rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Multi-year policies are around 50% of the fresh book; good agents are paid upfront under Indian GAAP and the amount is deferred under IFRS; clarification is awaited on whether years two and three count as fresh or renewal under the new rules.

risks_watch: Optical moderation of fresh growth in Q3 and Q4 as the GST-driven base builds.

IRDAI distribution reform (commission linked to renewal rates, agent exclusivity, higher rural commissions) and whether the EoM cap of 20% can be met without major OpEx changes; the calculation was not disclosed.
Treatment of multi-year policy commissions (years two and three) under the new distribution rules; about 50% of fresh book is multi-year.
Dark-pattern and data consent norms for D2C, which is growing rapidly.
Supreme Court drug-pricing order and its effect on itemized hospital bills (about 20% of claims are non-package).
Investment book sensitivity to rising yields and a planned RBI policy rate hike cycle.

543413|2026-03.headline: Tega Q4 FY26: FY26 revenue up 5% to INR17,736 mn, adjusted EBITDA 22%; consumables flat as orders slipped to Feb–Mar, and Molycop acquisition closed 1 June 2026.
543413|2026-03.overview: Tega reported FY26 revenue of INR17,736 mn (up 5% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR3,967 mn (22% margin), after exceptional items of INR775 mn (Molycop deal costs) and INR64 mn (labour code), with a further INR839 mn total labour-code charge cited. Equipment grew 25% to INR2,688 mn for FY26. The Molycop acquisition completed on 1 June 2026 with Apollo Funds as a minority partner; consolidation starts from Q1 FY27, and management flagged about USD30 mn of transaction costs payable in Q1 and a target of 3x leverage in 3 to 4 years.

543420|2026-09.headline: Jet Freight H1 FY27 revenue about ₹297 Cr, with PAT margin near 1.5% and management guiding FY27 revenue to ₹580–600 Cr.
543420|2026-09.overview: Management presented H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) revenue of about ₹297 Cr, with EBITDA margin of about 4.58% and PAT margin of about 1.52% (CFO also cited 1.55%). Shipments rose from 430 to 674 and tonnage from 545 to 744 tons year on year, with tonnage up about 32.84%. Management said it expects to close FY27 at ₹580–600 Cr revenue and targets roughly double the PAT margin, with H1 EBITDA cited as ₹12.5 Cr. Strategic items discussed were a proposed Dubai acquisition (NatWest), retail courier launch, ocean freight build-out, South America entry and a planned booking platform.

segments.commentary: About 45% of revenue; management calls it a niche, time-sensitive business where the company is the largest in India by volume, including mangoes to US and UK and roses.

segments.commentary: Courier and e-commerce estimated at 25–30% of general cargo volumes; 98% of business is international per management.

segments.name: Ocean freight
segments.commentary: Small today (sea imports described as negligible); centralised in a Delhi team and targeted for growth in bulk and rice, with no revenue target given.

segments.name: Air import and sea import
segments.commentary: Described as negligible; management plans to build these over time.

qa_highlights.answer: Courier sits within general cargo. Management said ocean freight must be pursued for sheer scale, but it will be taken slowly.

qa_highlights.answer: The target (NatWest) covers UAE, Gulf and Saudi. Valuation was based on future orders from its promoters' linked customers. The deal is not complete, so no FY27 impact is expected.

qa_highlights.answer: Ocean team is centralised in Delhi; relationships with about 8–9 major shipping lines. No medium-term revenue target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 41% Q2 YoY revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: No split was given. Management cited a sales process for volume growth and route-specific pricing, with fuel costs affecting freight rates.

qa_highlights.question: Courier shipments and tonnage decreased YoY; what is the driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth to new routes (direct flights to destinations like Germany), new e-commerce customers and organic growth at existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil/South America: current stage and milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: A senior person hired in Brazil; inquiries have turned into some business. Own operations are possible in about a year once volumes increase.

qa_highlights.answer: No land is owned and all warehouses are leased. Management expects margins and bottom line to rise quarter on quarter as costs stay flat.

543425|2026-03.headline: MapmyIndia Q4 FY26: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA margin 44.6% (+460 bps YoY), but FY26 revenue only INR474 crore vs INR463 crore.
543425|2026-03.overview: Management reported a sharp sequential Q4 recovery: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA up 141% QoQ, PAT up 171% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 44.6% and PAT margin at 31.3%. Full-year FY26 growth was muted, with revenue moving from INR463 crore to INR474 crore, as government contracts were delayed or deferred into FY27. Management attributed the Q4 shortfall against its own expectations (about INR45-50 crore by an analyst's estimate) to customer-side delays of roughly INR20 crore in an automotive IoT order plus government push-outs, all described as timing rather than lost business. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY28 roadmap and an order book of about INR1,750 crore, but gave no formal FY27 growth guidance.

segments.commentary: Grew about 9% for FY26 per management. Q4 automotive core business described as soft by an analyst; management said a Hyundai-related variation was a drag, while attach rates and program presence rose YoY.

segments.commentary: Declined about 3% for FY26, which management attributed to government contracts delayed into FY27. C&E rose 142% QoQ in Q4. Government open order book closed above INR200 crore; government billing crossed INR100 crore and cash collection crossed INR100 crore in FY26.

segments.name: IoT-led business
segments.commentary: Management said IoT EBITDA margin rose from 14% in FY25 to 16% in FY26, with Q4 margin at about 33%. Management called this a quarterly high driven by operating leverage and a better SaaS mix, not a one-off.

Management said a government 'Large Energy response system' order and a large government IoT tender (re-tendered) were delayed, outside its control.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a weak full-year performance in automotive/mobility and consumer-enterprise, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total FY26 revenue was INR474 crore vs INR463 crore; C&E fell about 3% because government work was delayed and A&M grew about 9%. Q4 C&E rose 142% QoQ. The government order book is above INR200 crore, and management is confident of significant growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book to revenue conversion outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 conversion was about 18% of the INR1,500 crore opening book. Management declined to give a fixed range but said FY27 could be higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan for the roughly INR600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic growth comes first (IoT, government, IP). IoT hardware is capitalised and depreciated over 3 years, and government needs working capital. No acquisition, dividend or buyback plan was detailed beyond the FY26 final dividend.

qa_highlights.question: Where was the Q4 revenue shortfall of about INR45-50 crore vs expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly INR20 crore automotive IoT order delayed by customer regulatory requirements (now fulfilled, expected in Q1-Q2), a government Large Energy Response order delayed by the government, and a large government IoT tender sent to re-tender. Management called these push-outs, not lost business.

qa_highlights.question: Why is core C&E flat, and will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the corporate API/SDK revenue ramps with usage (Amazon Now cited), with a gestation period. Segment reporting will move to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government from Q1 FY27 with restated quarterly FY26 figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and is there a collection concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government receivables reflect a longer collection cycle with no material bad debt; Mappls DT collected prior-year receivables, with overdue amounts expected to be lower than total receivables. DSO was described as better than industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IoT margins rise to about 33% in Q4 and is inventory a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to operating leverage, better mix (more SaaS) and cost optimisation, and denied inventory gains. Inventory rose to meet expected IoT demand. Management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27.

543425|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14.9% YoY to INR139.7 crore and EBITDA margin was 40.2%, despite a one-time INR4 crore government receivable write-off.
543425|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14.9% YoY to INR139.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR56.1 crore (40.2% margin) and PAT up 8.6% to INR49.7 crore (31.2% margin). Management said a one-time write-off of a government client's receivable (about INR4 crore gross, INR0.8 crore net P&L hit after a INR3.2 crore offset) cut the EBITDA margin by roughly 4 percentage points, with the balance sitting in other income. The company moved to a new three-segment reporting structure (Automotive, Enterprise, Government) and appointed Rohan Verma as Joint MD. IoT-led revenue rose sharply while Map-led revenue was nearly flat, and management attributed Automotive softness in FY26 H2 to OEM time-shifting rather than contract loss.

segments.name: Enterprise

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated an internal target of 35%+ EBITDA margin for FY27 and declined to guide quarter-by-quarter; asked about 43-44% margins, it said quarterly outcomes will vary.

Open order book at FY26 end was INR1,750 crore, up from INR1,500 crore a year earlier (and about INR1,350 crore before that); management cited it as visibility for future growth but would not comment on quarterly revenue.
Management expects Automotive contract volumes to recover as OEMs change vehicle programmes, but gave no quantitative FY27 Automotive growth target.
International: Southeast Asia JV loss reduced; international revenue not material to P&L in the near term; smaller investments in Middle East and other geographies.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning figures were discussed on the call.
IoT hardware-first growth is expected to convert into SaaS revenue over time, per management.
demand_pricing: Order book split disclosed only annually as fixed-price versus volume-based; not disclosed quarterly for competitive reasons.
Pricing is bespoke, per vehicle, per API transaction, per user or per solution; contract tenure ranges from one to five years with no typical term.
Management said receivables from government are a longer cycle than Automotive and Enterprise; majority of FY26 receivables of INR176 crore were from government (exact share not given).
Digital twin cities opportunity (including Maharashtra's NAKSHA scheme) is being pursued selectively to avoid bad receivables seen at peers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Automotive OEM contract reduction a 2H FY26 event, and could 2H FY27 be better on a weaker base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not a contract reduction but time-shifting: one OEM chose not to deploy the technology in some vehicles last year, which may continue, though more vehicles are expected to carry the technology in future.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin run at 43-44% in coming quarters excluding the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 35%+ full-year margin target and said quarterly margins will vary.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone Map-led growth so low and subsidiary revenue down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated numbers should be used, as Government and IoT work is routed through subsidiaries; consolidated Map-led was flat at INR98.7 crore while IoT-led rose to INR41 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Order book mix by segment and e-commerce deal progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book split by segment was not disclosed; the fixed versus volume split is given annually. Management cited quick commerce and other enterprise wins without quantifying them.

qa_highlights.question: Reconcile the write-off: INR80 lakh P&L impact vs 4% EBITDA margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The gross INR4 crore receivable was offset by a INR3.2 crore payable not paid; the net INR0.8 crore went to other expense, while the payable saving sat in other income, so the EBITDA margin was hit by about 4 points.

qa_highlights.question: Is IoT services revenue seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IoT services follow hardware sales with a lag and billing cycles vary (monthly to biennial), so sequential comparisons mislead; Q1 FY27 IoT services INR18 crore vs INR16.3 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is there material international revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said international revenue is not material and the Southeast Asia JV loss has reduced.

risks_watch: Government receivables: longer collection cycle and a one-time write-off this quarter; watch the government receivable balance and any further write-offs.
Map-led revenue flat YoY at INR98.7 crore; growth is now dependent on IoT-led and Automotive recovery.
IoT hardware-led growth carries lower margin until SaaS converts; margin dilution expected to persist as IoT scales.
Automotive OEM programme timing: continued time-shifting could keep the segment below its potential in the near term.
Southeast Asia JV and other international investments remain loss-making with no near-term material revenue.

543426|2026-03.headline: Metro Brands Q4 FY26: standalone revenue up 20%, PAT up 18%, FY26 delivered within guidance (sales +15%, PAT mid-teens) despite slow start.
543426|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone growth of 20% with EBITDA up 20% and PAT up 18%, and said FY26 metrics landed in guidance after a slow start to the year. Digital commerce grew 53% and reached 12% of revenue in the quarter. The company ended the quarter with 1,032 stores after a net addition of 42, and opened its first two FILA stores since the acquisition. Management flagged input cost inflation from the Gulf crisis (around 10% on affected items), which it plans to mitigate through forward buying and pre-built inventory of about six months.

segments.commentary: Management cited footfall growth and rising bills in Metro stores, with revenue per square foot held at 4,500 sq ft across Q3 to Q4. Management said same-store growth (SSG) is the main driver of growth, not just new stores, and believes it is gaining market share.

segments.name: Digital commerce (e-commerce and omnichannel)
segments.commentary: Grew 53% in Q4 and made up 12% of revenue. Management expects it to stay in a 12% to 15% share of business in the near term, with lumpiness around festive periods.

segments.commentary: Two stores opened since acquisition. Management spent time and money clearing old inventory and is repositioning the brand with local manufacturing, expecting it to be meaningful to numbers in about 18 months.

Management said footwear is infrequent and not a high-ticket purchase, limiting demand sensitivity to inflation.
Men's and unisex category shifts were attributed to reclassification by third-party brands; combined mix unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How much is input cost inflation and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nissan Joseph put input cost inflation at around 10% on affected items, mitigated by bulk forward buying and six months of inventory; no knee-jerk price hikes, only normal inflation. Kaushal Parekh said higher inventory reflects front-loading ahead of the price rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth driven by SSG or new stores, and what is footfall trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSG is the main driver along with new stores and annualisation; revenue per sq ft held at 4,500 sq ft; in-store footfall and new customer acquisition improved through the back half of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term growth outlook for FY27 and store pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50 stores are available across FILA, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv in FY27, but BIS, rentals and timing remain uncertain; growth of around 15% is targeted long-term, with no quarter-by-quarter commitment.

qa_highlights.question: When will Foot Locker BIS issues and FILA repositioning normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not predict BIS clearance timing; FILA repositioning takes time with inventory clean-up, and management expects it to be meaningful in about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company out of the hyper-competitive rental market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not out of it, but the acceleration in rental competition has stabilised.

risks_watch: BIS certification uncertainty for Foot Locker and MetroActiv, which depend on imported products; management said it is a constraint on store openings.
Input cost inflation of about 10% on certain categories linked to crude and the Gulf crisis; pricing response is yet to be determined.
FILA turnaround timeline (about 18 months) and cleared inventory costs.

543426|2026-06.headline: Metro Brands Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 14% and PAT about 13%, with April-May soft and June recovering to mid-teens-plus growth.
543426|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 14% and EBITDA 9% in Q1 FY27, with PAT up 13%, per management's opening remarks. April and May were soft on the U.S.-Iran conflict overhang and a shift in wedding dates, while June rebounded to a mid-teen double-digit gain. The e-commerce SOR (3P) channel slowed to 9%, while D2C and marketplace omni each grew about 60%. Management reiterated gross margin near 55-57% (quarter at almost 60%), EBITDA around 30%, and full-year PAT of 13-15%, citing marketing, treasury income, new-store dilution and talent/tech investment as PAT margin drivers.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Opened 3 new EBOs and closed 1 legacy store (of 2 inherited); management said the brand is behind schedule, with acceleration expected toward end of FY27.

segments.name: MetroActiv / Walkway
segments.commentary: MetroActiv: 3 stores opened, 2 doing well and 1 underperforming, with BIS issues cited. Walkway: base of about 70 stores, over 30 opened in the quarter (about 50% growth), with mixed store performance.

segments.commentary: Growth was weaker pre-monsoon because June 2025 had strong monsoon demand that did not repeat in June 2026; management said Crocs is performing to plan now.

Demand described as broad-based across price points, geographies and banners; management said it is not seeing it driven only by metros or Tier-3 cities.
Gross margin held near 60% through inventory discipline and forward buying 4-5 months ahead; normal inflationary price increases of 3-5%, with no direct oil-price impact yet.
Realisations up 6% YoY, mainly from mix (newer premium formats and Crocs), with full-year ASP growth expected at about 3-4%.
Premium 3,000+ price band at about 57% of sales (management said it is approaching 60%), with premiumisation expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why were April and May muted when peers held up, and was June materially stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited zero wedding dates in April and May and a consumer-sentiment distraction from the prolonged war. June rebounded strongly, helped by Crocs-friendly monsoon absence offset by other brands; the Crocs shortfall was timing-related.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SOR (3P) e-commerce slow, and will discounting cut growth?
qa_highlights.answer: SOR growth was lumpy from return-swap timing, plus a deliberate reduction in low price points and 3P discounts. Management expects e-com to grow well into double digits, with 20-30% a year as the healthy range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year margin outlook given wage hikes and input cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided gross margin 55-57% (currently above), EBITDA around 30%, and PAT 13-15%. Front-end wages are above state minimums, but wage rules will be absorbed as they change.

qa_highlights.question: Why not guide to 20% growth when demand is improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers measured guidance to avoid inventory overhang and brand-share loss; it guides to about 15% and says it aims higher. It cited three quarters of steady double-digit growth and rising conversion and new-customer counts.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the PAT margin decline and when does PAT growth return to mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 bps from top-of-funnel marketing, plus lower treasury income versus last year's teens yields, new-store dilution (about 40 Walkway stores among 140 openings), and talent/tech investment. Management expects a return to 15%-plus PAT growth as these normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Is BIS relief helping FILA launch timelines, and how is FILA inventory being discounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recent QC order allowing imports has no significant impact; ASEAN BIS renewals are the larger constraint. Heavy FILA discounting reflects legacy acquired inventory and 3-4 month sports life cycles with 9-month buying lead times.

risks_watch: BIS certification erraticism for factories, especially ASEAN suppliers and high-end athletic footwear, could constrain FILA and sports launches.

Minimum wage increases in certain states could raise front-end staff costs.

Diwali shift into Q3 could weigh on Q2 growth; FILA turnaround timing (late FY27) and MetroActiv and Walkway store productivity are open questions.

543426|2026-09.headline: Metro Brands Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12.2% to INR730 crore, with EBITDA up 15.9% to INR198 crore, while festive demand shifted into Q3.
543426|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.2% to INR730 crore and EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR198 crore, with margin at 27.1% versus 26.2% a year ago. PAT grew about 11% to INR77 crore with margin flat at 10.6%, as higher rentals, staff costs and marketing, plus lower treasury income, offset a gross margin gain. Management attributed much of the revenue slowdown to festive demand moving from September into October, and said net store additions were slowed to 12 in Q2 with selective openings. Newer brands (Clarks, Foot Locker, MetroActiv, FILA) remain constrained by BIS-related supply issues and are being scaled cautiously.

financial_highlights.change: lower vs prior strong treasury year; FY26 full-year other income about INR100 crore

segments.name: Metro / Mochi / Walkway / own brands
segments.commentary: Own brands contributed about 70% of store product sales at Metro, Mochi and Walkway in H1. Walkway: over 35 stores opened in last 12-14 months on a base of about 60-70; roughly 30% performed well, 30% average, 30% poor.

segments.name: Crocs
segments.commentary: Crocs is under 20% of total business across stores, Metro and Mochi multi-brand. Management said Crocs grew decently and Durga Puja/Shraddh timing, not Crocs, drove the quarter.

segments.name: Clarks
segments.commentary: Women's range in more than 400 multi-brand outlets and limited men's range in more than 100; full exclusive store range expected in Q3 FY27, exclusive EBO launch targeted in H2 FY27. Clarks had about 80 EBOs in India at one point.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Local footwear manufacturing started in India in response to BIS concerns; repositioning expected over 12-18 months, with store expansion picking up from FY28.

segments.name: Foot Locker / MetroActiv

543458|2026-03.headline: AWL Agri Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 21,000+ crore (+18% YoY) on 14% volume growth to ~1.9 MMT; EBITDA per ton ~INR 3,400.
543458|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue, with volume up 14% to about 1.9 million tonnes and operational EBITDA of INR 628 crore (+40% YoY). Edible oil volume grew 17% and Food/FMCG about 6%, while Industry Essentials grew 13%. Management flagged that the March 2026 Iran conflict pushed crude-linked input costs (packaging, chemicals, coal) and edible oil prices higher, with the cost impact expected to hit Q1 FY27 rather than Q4. April demand was sluggish, with management expecting recovery in May and June.

segments.name: Edible Oil
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +17% YoY and revenue INR 17,520 crore (+19% YoY); FY26 volume +6%. Market share up 60 bps in Q4; e-com and quick commerce share held above 30%.

segments.name: Food and FMCG
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +6% (about +3% normalised for FY26 G2G exit); FY26 volume -4% reported, +3%+ normalised. Basmati rice share up 330 bps to near 9%; wheat flour share flat at 5.3-5.4%. Segment profit about INR 35 crore in Q4 and about INR 200 crore for FY26.

segments.name: Industry Essentials
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +13% and revenue +11% YoY; FY26 volume +8%. Oleo chemicals are about 30% of the segment; specialty chemicals about 7-8% of portfolio. New Krishnapatnam capacity expected by early Q4 FY27.

segments.name: GD Foods (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +24% and revenue +21%; FY26 volume +15% and revenue +12%. Material margin about 55% in Q4 and 54% for FY26.

guidance_outlook: Food volume growth targeted at mid-teens (double digit) in FY27; top line prioritised over margins through FY27 and possibly part of FY28.
Food to stay EBITDA neutral until FY27; INR 1,500-2,000/ton EBITDA targeted from FY28, subject to scale of ~1.5-1.6 MMT food volume (FY26 about 1.2 MMT).
Steady-state EBITDA per ton guided at about INR 3,500-3,600 (safer end INR 3,500).
Q1 FY27 expected to absorb cost inflation from packaging, chemicals, coal and crude-linked inputs; price corrections planned toward end-April.
Management expects May and June demand to recover; Q1 described as good overall despite weak April. Edible oil and foods growth stated as single-digit, not double-digit, for Q1 per Q&A.
Indonesia B50 biodiesel plan from H2 2026 may firm palm prices and narrow spreads versus soft oils, seen as positive for AWL.
capex_capacity: Krishnapatnam oleo-chemical installation expected by early Q4 FY27 to add Industry Essentials volume.
Food volume at ~1.2 MMT in FY26; management hopes to exceed 1.5-1.6 MMT in FY27 to start consolidating food margins.
Direct outlet reach about 970,000; direct plus indirect reach 2.6 million (Nielsen), against a universe of more than 4 million outlets.
demand_pricing: Edible oil complex rose about 10% in March 2026 on the Iran conflict; sunflower above $1,400/t, soya near $1,300/t, palm $1,220-1,250/t. Industry passed this on to consumers in mid-to-late March.
Packaging is about 2-3% of cost; a 10-15% rise implies roughly 25-50 bps margin impact per quarter. Price correction planned for end-April.
Management estimates demand falls about 1% for every INR 10 rise in oil prices.
Alternate channel grew 43% YoY in Q4 (about 15% of edible oil volume, about 25% of food volume); HoReCa +64%; branded exports +48%; masstige brands +18% volume; Kohinoor +39%.
Alternate channel margin estimated only 50-60 bps above general trade; overall company EBITDA margin around 1.5-2%.
Wheat flour competition from smaller private-label players in FY26 as wheat prices were range-bound; wheat firming could help organised players.
Rupee depreciation in March and elevated freight/vessel availability cited as headwinds for imports and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company gain or lose from the Iran crisis (gas/LPG disruption to HoReCa, edible oil inflation, convenience food upstocking)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 impact was limited because March trade stocking offset price effects; LPG-driven demand destruction was brief, but April demand was sluggish as stocked inventory was consumed.

qa_highlights.question: Food margin sustainability after restructuring and whether FY26 is a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Food profitability depends on top-line opportunity; priority is volume through FY27, with current margin levels maintained and possibly more aggressive pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Food volume and margin trade-off, and AOP base case?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case is double-digit, mid-teens food volume growth in FY27; margins may be slightly lower (versus about 3% margin in FY26) if opportunities arise, with wheat flour as the key upside.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state EBITDA per ton and sensitivity to oil price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state about INR 3,500-3,600/ton. Demand slows about 1% per INR 10 price increase; inventory is managed against international prices and season.

qa_highlights.question: Palm oil plantation plans and Indonesian B50 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans for plantations; Wilmar parent holds palm plantations. B50 from H2 2026 may lift palm prices and narrow spreads, positive for soft-oil-focused AWL.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide margin per ton rather than percentage, and why is valuation low versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-ton guidance reflects that brand pricing passes through commodity moves, so percentage margins fall while per-ton margins hold. Management said valuation is market-driven and classed the company as food FMCG (70% of revenue from brands).

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin pressure from packaging, chemical, coal and crude-linked cost inflation following the Iran conflict.
Weak April demand; recovery in May-June is needed for Q1 to hold up.
Food volume-over-margin strategy may compress food margins against a targeted INR 1,500-2,000/ton from FY28.
Edible oil price volatility and demand elasticity (about 1% per INR 10 move); palm and B50 policy effects.
Interim CFO in place; trade credit versus borrowings shifts and rupee depreciation affect working capital and import costs.
Standalone food volume de-grew in FY26 and the wheat/rice competitive environment remains open.

543458|2026-06.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 20,048 crore and operating EBITDA 34% to INR 693 crore in Q1 FY27, with Edible Oil volume only 2%.
543458|2026-06.overview: AWL Agri Business reported broad-based growth in Q1 FY27, with consolidated revenue up 18% YoY to INR 20,048 crore on 7% underlying volume growth. Operating EBITDA rose 34% to INR 693 crore, with PBT up 48% and PAT up 40%, which management attributed to a Food-led mix, disciplined pricing and efficiencies. Edible Oil volume grew only 2% due to channel destocking and supply chain issues amid palm oil volatility, while Industry Essentials grew volume 13%. Management said July trends had improved and reiterated FY27 segment operating guidance, and changed segment disclosure to revenue, volume growth and margin for Food and FMCG.

financial_highlights.metric: Alternate channels (modern trade, e-com, quick commerce)

segments.name: Food and FMCG

segments.name: Edible Oil
segments.commentary: Volume up 2% YoY due to channel destocking, supply chain disruption and sluggish trade; revenue up 15% and EBITDA per ton up 33% YoY.

segments.name: Industry Essentials

Edible Oil: volume growth of about 5%-6% for the remaining nine months of FY27; EBITDA expected at INR 4,000-4,500 per ton.
Industry Essentials: volume growth of about 8%-9%; EBITDA expected at INR 3,000-3,500 per ton.

Madhur: target to scale from about 15,000 tons/month to about 20,000 tons/month by year end; FY27 revenue from the brand estimated at INR 700-800 crore; royalty of 0.5% of sales payable to Shree Renuka Sugars.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry (Jefferies): What revenue, growth and EBITDA margin should be expected for Food and FMCG for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided double-digit volume and revenue growth, with revenue growth of about 18%-20%; the 6% Q1 margin should not be the benchmark, and the average of the last four to five quarters is the right yardstick given the investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry: What revenue, margin and royalty terms apply to Madhur, and what are the targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Madhur sells about 15,000 tons/month, targeted at 20,000 tons/month by year end; FY27 revenue estimated at INR 700-800 crore; royalty 0.5% of sales to Shree Renuka Sugars; margin guidance to be in line with the overall Food segment.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry: What Edible Oil volume growth is expected over the medium term and full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume was hit by destocking, supply chain issues and sluggish trade; management is not guiding 2% and expects 5%-6% volume growth over the remaining nine months, with festive and post-monsoon demand from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Joytiraditya (ICICI Securities): What capex and market share gains are budgeted for the 2030 vision?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific four-year capex figure; capex will follow capacity needs, with Edible Oil refining at 60%-61% utilisation likely exhausted in a couple of years. Steady-state modelling assumption is about INR 700 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Joytiraditya: What efficiencies will the higher Wilmar ownership bring, and how much can domestic oilseed sourcing reduce imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing efficiency is unchanged; the main new lever is Wilmar's R&D and technical expertise. Management declined to give an import-reduction number, noting about 70% of edible oil requirement is imported and mustard is the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Lakshmi Narayan (Tunga Investments): What share of raw material is imported and from Wilmar, and what is the volume growth outlook? Also, B2C/B2B mix of Food?

qa_highlights.question: Lakshmi Narayan: How are Wilmar transactions priced and what are the stock days and oil mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Wilmar transactions are at arm's length, including pricing and credit period. Raw material stock is 30-35 days; oil mix is about 30% palm, 30%-35% soya, 20% sunflower and 15% local oils.

543514|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to about INR150 crore and enrollments rose 35% to about 1.03 lakh students. EBITDA was about INR54 crore with a margin near 36% as stated, but management acknowledged the reported EBITDA growth of 10% was flattered by a INR17 crore one-time other income in Q1 FY26; excluding it, EBITDA grew about 30%. PAT rose to INR34 crore from INR5.9 crore, helped by a INR7.35 crore tax reversal tied to an intra-group merger. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR670 crore revenue, INR260 crore EBITDA and INR144 crore PAT, and said the Commerce demerger NCLT order is expected shortly with listing before end-September 2026.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven last quarter. Target of INR95-100 crore EBITDA over four to five years; Karnataka expansion planned in FY27.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.2 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR9.2 crore (+53% YoY). Manages six schools with over 5,400 students; preschool managed operations to be entered in FY27.

Commerce positioned as number one across CA, CS, CMA, ACCA; management claims undisputed leadership in pedigree, alumni, centres and ranks.

543517|2026-03.headline: Hariom Pipe FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR1,667 crore and EBITDA 19% to INR209 crore at a 12.56% margin, with FY27 volume guided at 350,000-360,000 tonnes.

FY26 volume growth fell short of the 30% guided last year, as management prioritised margin and cash over volume. Management said a Tamil Nadu (Perundurai) plant closure linked to a pollution board order had not yet hit volumes, citing stock and asset-light supply, and that reopening was expected within days.

543523|2026-03.headline: Campus Activewear Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, EBITDA margin 19.2%, FY26 PAT margin 8.4%.
543523|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 12.3% YoY to INR 456 crore, led by online (around 19%) and distribution (around 5.5%). EBITDA was INR 88.5 crore at a 19.2% margin (up 50 bps) and PAT was INR 44.1 crore at a 9.6% margin (up 100 bps). For FY26, revenue grew 11.4% to INR 1,774 crore, EBITDA margin rose 145 bps to 17.5%, and PAT margin rose 80 bps to 8.4%. Management said the mid-year raw material and minimum wage inflation was passed on via MRP hikes taken in early April, and that demand held up in April.

segments.name: Online (marketplace)
segments.commentary: Online grew about 19% in Q4 and 9.8% in FY26; management said all online business is pure marketplace except Flipkart, with Amazon, Snapdeal and brand.com growing faster. Online salience rose in Q4, though GT charges dilute gross margin and billing changed from 16 June to net of freight (INR 82 billed against INR 100 earlier).

segments.name: Distribution (general trade and franchise)
segments.commentary: Distribution grew about 5.5% in Q4 and 10.5% in FY26. Management said the annual distribution meet produced strong four-month forward orders, with AOP alignments with partners closed at over 100% of the target till September.

segments.name: Sneakers
segments.commentary: Sneaker portfolio grew about 100% YoY in FY26 and more than 50% in quarterly terms; the Paonta Sahib and Pant Nagar units are producing about 2 lakh pairs per month, targeted to double by end FY27. Management did not disclose sneaker revenue or volume share.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated its EBITDA margin aspiration band of 17% to 19% for FY27 but gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
Management said pricing taken in early April covers the inflation impact and that raw material prices have peaked and are starting to ease; no further price hikes expected.
Plan to open 60 to 80 new EBO stores in FY27 (about 40% COCO and 60% FOFO), after closing 9 to 10 and opening 13 to 14 stores in FY26; store count stood at about 300.
Marketing budget for FY27 set to be aggressive, focused on brand building rather than performance marketing.

Capex in FY27 expected to return to normal maintenance, mold, EBO and IT levels; Pant Nagar expansion including assembly lines is planned over the next three years, after first optimising the upper facility.
Full BIS compliance expected by 31 July 2026, with very little BIS stock remaining.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share of shoes priced below INR 1,000 rise versus Q4 FY25, and is the pricing MRP or realised price?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the figures are realised ASP; the shift reflects MRP corrections after GST on footwear was revised from 12% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What size of price hike was taken and will it suffice against inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO declined to give the percentage, said hikes were taken proportionately across the range and are enough to cover raw material and minimum wage inflation; peak RM seen, prices to ease in about a quarter, with no price reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses (ex-ad spend) rise only about 5% despite online growth of 19%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited dynamic online commission negotiations and event-based waivers, plus flat store count meaning no new EBO costs; other costs grew in the 5-6% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lease cash outflow rise sharply, nearly 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the Pant Nagar land is a 71-year state government lease treated as lease liability payment; normalised FY26 rent excluding INR 65.4 crore is the base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise 5-6 days in FY26 and where will they go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FG inventory was at a very minimal level last year and was rebuilt to the right level by March 2026, which will be maintained going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for sneaker growth, and what is the path to 2 lakh pairs a month?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said capacity is not a constraint now; Pant Nagar can reach 6 lakh pairs per month after two phases and HRD2 can reach 2 lakh (already running), targeting 8-9 lakh pairs per month in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins reach the 17-19% band or slip to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; CEO said the company will endeavour to stay within the 17-19% range guided earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBO expansion plan and capex for stores and facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said 60-70 or about 80 new stores are planned after closing 9-10 and opening 13-14 in FY26; CFO said FY27 capex reverts to normal maintenance, mould, EBO and IT levels, with Pant Nagar expansion over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What were the distribution meet outcomes and demand trend?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said order bookings were strong on a four-month forward basis, numbers not shared; COO said AOP alignments with distributors were closed at over 100% till September.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the low Q4 ASP growth of 1.5% when D2C/online realisations should be higher?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to online billing change from 16 June (INR 82 billed against INR 100) with freight of INR 18 billed directly by portals, which is not in last year's Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the BIS compliance position?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the company is hardly left with any non-BIS stock and expects full compliance by 31 July 2026; the reported BIS rethink is only chatter with no official communication.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company gaining share in competitive affordable athleisure, and what are its moats?
qa_highlights.answer: COO cited an integrated supply chain, strongest distribution network, R&D, 20-year brand loyalty; CEO estimated replicating the supply chain would need about INR 2,000 crore.

capex_capacity: Sneaker capacity: Paonta Sahib upper facility stabilised; Pant Nagar unit production commenced; combined output about 2 lakh pairs per month, targeted to double by end FY27.

FY27 capex to return to normal range: plant routine maintenance, mould, EBO store additions and IT infra; FY26 was elevated by the Pant Nagar acquisition. Pant Nagar expansion incl. assembly lines over next three years, after first optimising the upper facility at Pant Nagar.
